doc.meta.goal: Second service sub-plan for the parent plan prune-dangling-hook-references-v7. After the first sub-plan (agentctl-venue-propagation, landed 7b3a624) fixed the venue fields, `pop-subplan` restored the parent at EXECUTING with its venue correct — but left parent stage 2 UNREACHABLE. cmd_pop_subplan restores the parent's stages in full, including a stage still marked ACTIVE, and then unconditionally sets state.current_stage = None (cli.py:3305). No engine verb re-enters that stage: next-stage selects only PENDING stages whose deps are PASSED (state.py:1092-1099) and so reports 'no ready stages'; dispatch and record-result both act only through active_stage(), which returns None when current_stage is None (cli.py:2129-2131, 2242-2246); replan re-arms only FAILED stages, and only inside DIAGNOSING (cli.py:3098-3101, 3118-3119), which cannot be entered because entering it requires record-result on an active stage. The parent stage is therefore unreachable by every ORDINARY verb. It is not literally unrecoverable: `replan --kind substantive` (cli.py:3140-3147) rebuilds `state.stages` from a new plan file and carries forward only PASSED stages, so the ACTIVE stage would return as PENDING and `next-stage` could pick it up. That escape is real and this plan does not pretend otherwise — it is rejected on COST, not impossibility: it re-arms the parent's plan-approval hard gate, spending a full user re-approval of an unchanged 5-stage plan plus a paid thinker plan-review, to work around an engine defect that will re-wedge the next sub-plan pop. This is the SAME structural family as the defect the first sub-plan closed: two representations of one fact that must move together are moved apart. Here the pair is the stage-status ACTIVE and the redundant pointer current_stage. PlanFrame even captures current_stage (state.py:720) and its docstring promises the parent 'resumes exactly where it left off' (state.py:701-704); cmd_pop_subplan contradicts its own frame contract by discarding the field it snapshotted.

doc.stages[1].subject.invariants: The pointer is DERIVED from stage status, never restored verbatim from the frame — the frame this session must unwedge carries a None pointer next to an ACTIVE stage, so a verbatim restore would leave the parent exactly as blocked. ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING: the derivation must run AFTER the originating stage is marked PASSED at cli.py:3345. Placed before it, the common case (the originating stage IS the ACTIVE one) would re-enter an already-satisfied stage and would break the existing assertion at scripts/tests/test_subplan.py:189. The pair invariant it derives from is narrowed, deliberately, to any state CAPTURABLE IN A PlanFrame rather than asserted unconditionally: cmd_record_result's failed branch (cli.py:2484-2485) sets FAILED without clearing the pointer, so a pointer CAN reference a non-ACTIVE stage — but that write transitions to DIAGNOSING (cli.py:2496) and cmd_push_subplan refuses any node but EXECUTING (cli.py:3238-3242), so such a state can never enter a frame. Fail-safe in the ambiguous directions: zero ACTIVE stages or more than one both yield None, which is today's behaviour, so no new failure mode is introduced. The many-ACTIVE branch is dead-defensive and must NOT be claimed as tested: ACTIVE is written in exactly one place (cli.py:2082), reachable only from PARTITIONED/ROUTED/VERIFYING, never from EXECUTING, so two simultaneously-ACTIVE stages are unreachable rather than merely unobserved. No Node, no state-machine edge and no gate is added, changed or removed; the public CLI surface is unchanged; cmd_push_subplan is not touched. On this stage's own control instrument, probed CONJUNCT BY CONJUNCT rather than as a conjunction, because a short-circuiting chain hides a vacuous earlier conjunct behind a later failure: the two node-ids exit 4 today (no such tests exist); `_restore_current_stage` returns 0 hits repo-wide; `active-stage pointer` returns 0 hits in scripts/agentctl/README.md. The three-suite pytest conjunct exits 0 today and is therefore VACUOUS ON ITS OWN — it is retained only as a no-regression guard, which is why the node-id conjunct is placed FIRST.

doc.stages[1].subject.result: scripts/agentctl/cli.py defines a module-level helper named EXACTLY `_restore_current_stage` (a binding contract identifier: stage 3's landing instrument probes for it by name). Given the live state, it sets state.current_stage from the stages themselves: the index of the single stage whose outcome.status is ACTIVE, or None when there is no such stage or more than one (fail-safe — the current, safe behaviour). cmd_pop_subplan calls it in place of today's unconditional `state.current_stage = None` (cli.py:3305), AFTER the originating stage has been marked PASSED, so a pop whose originating stage was the active one correctly ends with no pointer. The rationale belongs in the code as a short comment: the ACTIVE status on the restored stages is the authoritative record of which stage is in flight and current_stage is a redundant pointer, so the pointer is DERIVED rather than trusted — the same reasoning the sibling helper `_sync_venue_from_plan` already applies when it prefers the parent plan file over the frame snapshot, because a frame captured after a value was already lost would keep it lost. That is exactly the case here: the frame this session pushed carries current_stage = None while its stage 2 is ACTIVE, so restoring frame.current_stage verbatim would NOT unwedge the parent, and deriving from status does. scripts/agentctl/README.md gains a short sentence stating the resulting invariant, containing the literal phrase `active-stage pointer`. Tests, two binding names in scripts/tests/test_subplan.py. The FIRST carries all the discriminating power and its shape is prescribed, not incidental: `test_pop_subplan_restores_pointer_to_active_stage` must push with an originating stage that is NOT the ACTIVE one (originating 1 while stage 2 is ACTIVE — the live parent's exact shape) and with frame.current_stage None, and must assert that after the pop current_stage equals the ACTIVE stage's index, state.active_stage() returns it, and the stage is re-enterable rather than stranded. The existing coverage cannot substitute for it: scripts/tests/test_subplan.py:189 is the only assertion in the suite pinning post-pop current_stage, it uses originating == the ACTIVE stage, and so it stays green under a correct fix AND under a no-op; test_roundtrip_with_plan_stack (:194) never pops, and test_pop_subplan_rederives_venue_from_plan (:371) pops without asserting the pointer. The SECOND, `test_pop_subplan_clears_pointer_when_originating_stage_was_active`, pins the other direction — when the ACTIVE stage IS the originating one, the pop marks it PASSED and leaves current_stage None with no stage left ACTIVE — which is also what guards the ordering requirement, since a derivation placed before the PASSED marking fails exactly here.

Its stage 2 could not run: agentctl dispatched the spawned developer into the read-only canonical checkout instead of the delivery worktree the plan declares, so the child refused all work and returned PERMISSION-REQUEST. Root cause, read from the code: state.repo_root and state.delivery_worktree are meant to be derived from the [meta] of state.plan_path, but only cmd_submit_plan sets both (cli.py:1358-1359). cmd_replan refreshes repo_root on BOTH its branches (cli.py:3091 refinement, cli.py:3116 substantive) and delivery_worktree on NEITHER; its no_change branch refreshes final_check for the in-place-edit case but no venue field at all; cmd_pop_subplan restores both from the PlanFrame snapshot (cli.py:3290-3291) rather than re-deriving them from the parent plan file, so a frame captured while the value was already lost keeps it lost; and — found by the first review of this sub-plan, not by the original diagnosis — _refresh_caches_from_plan_path (cli.py:232-273, called from cmd_approve:1862) is a FIFTH route with the same hole, and a strictly worse one: it re-loads the plan and refreshes state.final_check and every live stage's criterion fields INCLUDING verify_venue, while refreshing neither repo_root nor delivery_worktree. Its own docstring names the hazard in these very words — 'the gate attests to a plan it never actually executes' — and it is reachable by the engine's DESIGNED cycle (submit-plan -> present -> plan-review revise -> edit plan_path in place at the deliberately plan-mutable PLAN_READY -> present -> approve), which is exactly how a plan acquires a delivery_worktree it did not have at submit time. Plan v7 introduced delivery_worktree after submit-plan, reaching the session by replan, so the value never propagated and resolve_check_venue fell back to repo_root (state.py:1011). The engine gave no refusal and no warning at dispatch time. This reintroduces, through the replan route, exactly the venue asymmetry resolve_check_venue exists to remove.

It takes the live state and, optionally, an already-loaded plan document; when no document is passed it loads state.plan_path itself. It sets state.repo_root and state.delivery_worktree from that plan's [meta], TOGETHER, never one without the other. It is FAIL-SAFE: if the plan file is absent, unreadable or unparseable it leaves both existing values untouched and does not raise — a restore path must never crash the engine. It is called on every route that establishes, re-establishes or re-reads which plan the session is executing — FIVE call sites, enumerated from the code rather than assumed: (1) cmd_submit_plan, replacing today's two inline assignments at cli.py:1358-1359, with no behaviour change there; (2,3,4) all THREE branches of cmd_replan — no_change (which today refreshes stage fields and final_check for the in-place-edit case but no venue field), refinement (cli.py:3091), and substantive (cli.py:3116), each of which today refreshes repo_root alone; and (5) _refresh_caches_from_plan_path (cli.py:232-273), the approve-path refresh, whose miss is the worst of the set because it already copies each stage's verify_venue from the edited plan while leaving the state-level fields those venues resolve against stale. Site 5 keeps that function's existing best-effort contract: an absent or unloadable plan_path returns early and changes nothing. cmd_pop_subplan calls the helper AFTER restoring the parent frame, so the parent's venue is re-derived from the parent plan file, which is authoritative, and falls back to the frame's snapshotted values only when the helper cannot read that file; the PlanFrame fields stay in place as that fallback. cmd_push_subplan is DELIBERATELY not changed: it nulls both fields for the child on purpose, and no dispatch can occur before the child's own submit-plan refills them — with a comment stating that reason, so a future reader does not 'fix' it. scripts/agentctl/README.md gains a short statement of the resulting invariant containing the literal phrase `venue re-derivation`. Tests, three binding names: scripts/tests/test_replan.py gains `test_replan_refresh_delivery_worktree`, covering a replan that INTRODUCES [meta] delivery_worktree where the submitted plan had none, one that CHANGES it, and one that removes it — for the refinement, substantive and no_change diff kinds — asserting state.delivery_worktree matches the new plan each time and that repo_root keeps its existing correct behaviour. scripts/tests/test_subplan.py gains `test_pop_subplan_rederives_venue_from_plan`, covering: a parent whose live delivery_worktree was lost to None before the push still gets the plan-declared value back after pop; and a parent whose plan file is unreadable at pop time falls back to the frame values without raising. scripts/tests/test_check_venue.py — the suite that already owns venue behaviour — gains `test_approve_rederives_venue_from_edited_plan`, driving the engine's designed plan-review cycle end to end: submit a plan with no [meta] delivery_worktree, edit that same plan file IN PLACE at PLAN_READY to add one, approve, and assert state.delivery_worktree now matches the edited file and that resolve_check_venue(DELIVERY) returns it rather than repo_root.

doc.stages[4].subject.result: Three halves, all observed. (0) Creation — this is the half the user's original order names: the --init selector runs on the arc backend and produces a NEW registered project, not merely a working copy of an existing one. The exact invocation is `CLAUDE_PROJECT_INIT_BASE=<chosen base dir> enter-task.sh --init <scratch-name> --workspace arc` — --init takes the name as its OWN argument (enter-task.sh:65), so `--init --name <scratch>` would bind the selector argument to the literal string '--name' and die with 'unknown argument'; the destination is explicit rather than defaulted, because enter-task.sh:264 otherwise resolves the new project to `$PWD/<name>`, i.e. wherever the shell happened to be; and `--workspace arc` is explicit too, because without it a record auto-detected from the cwd (:109) outranks the identity default (:150 above :151) and an inferred name that fails to resolve falls back to git SILENTLY at :193-195 — so run from inside any registered git project, the creation half would seal a git commit, report success, and never touch arc. With the flag, a resolution failure dies loudly at :198 instead. The base dir is chosen from stage 2's INITTARGET verdict. enter-task.sh:205-208 refuses this half outright unless the backend defines both backend_init_workspace and backend_seal_workspace, so stage 2's INIT: verdict decides whether it can run at all; INIT: absent makes it RED here and routes to R6, it does not license quietly skipping it. Note that the init path also commits: enter-task.sh:296 calls backend_seal_workspace, whose meaning for a monorepo backend is read out in stage 2's SEAL: verdict before this half runs — and enter-task.sh:298-300 registers the new project itself with workspace_backend=arc, so no hand-written record is needed for it. (1) Entry: `claude-task <name>` creates a real arc working copy on this Mac and launches the agent with that copy as its cwd — the user sees a shell/session rooted in the monorepo working copy, and `arc info` (or the equivalent the client provides) run inside it reports a live mount. (2) Teardown: the workspace is removed with `arc unmount --forget` (plus --force if the registry entry is stale), after which the arc mount listing shows no WARN line for it and no store remains under ~/.arc/stores/ for that workspace. A short evidence file records all three halves so the final verification can confirm them without re-running anything: the exact --init invocation with its CLAUDE_PROJECT_INIT_BASE, the created project's path, the path of the registry record enter-task.sh:298-300 wrote and its workspace_backend field, the user's confirmation of the launched session's cwd, and the mount listing before and after.

The round's real contribution was a CLASSIFICATION I did not have: the repo's checks fall into FOUR classes by enumeration source, not one — (1) git index via `ls-files`, (2) staged diff under --staged, which is what pre-commit runs, (3) filesystem glob, for which staging is a harmless no-op, and (4) EXPLICIT MANIFEST. The invariant closes 1 and 2 and is redundant for 3. It cannot close 4, and class 4 is where the remaining defect lived. B4, verified by me on disk before folding: verify-config-root-refs is the hybrid — index-ENUMERATED but manifest-SATISFIED. Doc scope is every tracked file whose suffix is not .py/.sh, so both scripts/agentctl/README.md and the new principle leaf are in it; TILDE_RE carries a negative lookahead on the hyphen so `~/.claude-agent` is exempt; and agentctl/README.md carries ZERO matching occurrences today, meaning stage 6's prescribed section about 'the two config roots' would create the repo's FIRST one and fail hard. The criterion 'verify-config-root-refs stays green' was therefore unsatisfiable as written, and stage 6's Method actively misdirected by framing any red there as 'a genuine reference change to review' when the correct response is authoring a new allowlist row — structurally the same wrong-prediction error round 5 had already caught one surface over. The remedy is not a one-liner: the allowlist header requires an anchored `path:line:sha8` pin (sha8 = first 8 hex of sha256 over the stripped line), a mandatory categorized reason, and shipment in the SAME COMMIT as the file it governs (an entry added ahead of its file reads as stale in every clean checkout, 77ce06c). Stage 6 now states both admissible resolutions and prefers naming the literal with a `keep:harness-owned` row, since the reference IS to the harness's own root. Four non-blocking items folded too: re-stage after later edits (--staged validates the staged blob via `git show :path`, so a full-mode green over a stale index entry does not imply pre-commit green); stage 1 gained verify-semantic-gates for symmetry with 2-5; the 'close a MISSING by regenerating, never by an implementation change' remedy is now local to stages 3 and 4 rather than stated only twice elsewhere; and the principle leaf gained the sharper corollary this round paid for — a checker can be index-enumerated yet manifest-satisfied, so SURFACING an obligation is not DISCHARGING it, and a plan conflating the two produces a stage that is green precisely because nobody looked. Seven rounds, ~$18.7 and ~70 minutes. Note the shape of the last four: each found exactly one blocking defect of a single class, each fix was two sentences, and each round's fix created the surface the next round examined — the class is now closed at the level of a stated invariant plus its explicit limit, which is the first time the plan says what its own control does NOT cover. ROUND 8 (narrow, class-4/explicit-manifest sweep across the FULL check inventory) returned the first PASS after seven consecutive revises. It classified all 19 CHECKS members plus the three manifests reachable only through scripts/tests/ and the one advisory hook — 15 rows with a per-row ground — and found NO undeclared class-4 obligation: the four the plan does incur (crutch_registry.toml regeneration, the scripts/README.md sentinel row, the MEMORY.md index row, the config-root allowlist row) are each declared and each bounded to what its verifier actually enumerates. Four rows round 7 had missed were cleared with evidence rather than by assertion: test_no_semantic_unguarded's _KNOWN_UNGUARDED_HARD_SINKS is keyed by path+scope and never by content, so stage 5's docstring edit cannot disturb id 6b802bd6c3ae8553; gen_crutch_registry's CODE_ID_OVERRIDES exist only to contradict a partition and the partition table ends in a catch-all, so no new .py file needs a hand-authored row; lint-prose-length's GOVERNED set excludes scripts/README.md, scripts/agentctl/README.md and every memory leaf; and rule-salience-report --check-registry's domain is CLAUDE.md alone, which this plan forbids editing. It also settled the last open question by reading CODE_SUFFIXES: doc scope for verify-config-root-refs is the COMPLEMENT of .py/.sh, so every new .py file falls to the code-side enumerator whose allowlist-reason widening stage 1 already declares — no second manifest is implicated by the new code. Its five non-blocking refinements are folded above (A the missing type: key — the only one that would have produced a guaranteed red; B the deliberate stage-5-before-stage-6 regeneration order; C the why-safe ground of 6b802bd6c3ae8553 going stale silently as stage 4 widens gates.py's import closure; D preserve the three doc-bound headings; E use --repin rather than hand-computing a pin's sha8). All five were independently re-verified on disk before folding, as every round's claims have been: ALLOWED_TYPES and its hard failure at verify-memory-index.py:196-197; a grep returning ZERO allowlist pins for agentctl/README.md, principles/ or crutch_registry.toml; verify-onboarding-entrypoint's TARGETS being the REPO-ROOT README, not scripts/README.md; and doc-bindings.json's top-level concepts key. Eight rounds, ~$23. STRUCTURAL NOTE for the root, not a plan defect: a plan-review pass cannot bind without a --plan-digest the REVIEWER computed from its OWN read, and a spawned thinker can neither Read this path nor run shasum on it — so in this configuration a pass verdict can never be honestly recorded, and the user's override is the only truthful exit from the gate. That is the SAME defect class as this task's subject: a gate whose prover cannot reach the evidence it is asked to attest to.
doc.meta.goal: Let the engine SEE whether its own enforcement hooks will actually run in this session's harness config root, so a gate whose satisfier is absent diagnoses itself instead of emitting a generic refusal; and make every human escape from that gate record a TYPED reason so escape frequency becomes countable

Plus registry coverage in BOTH directions: every basename in the registry exists as a file in scripts/, AND every hook script in scripts/ that is GATE-BEARING is either in the registry or in an explicit justified exemption list. The gate-bearing predicate is 'denies OR writes an artifact some gate requires' — NOT 'denies' alone. That widening is load-bearing rather than pedantic: hook-plan-delivery-gate, the very hook this task exists for, mostly does not deny — it WRITES the delivery stamp that gates.plan_presentation_blockers requires — so a deny-only predicate would omit the task's own subject from the report built to find omissions. The deny half must still cover both mechanisms, PreToolUse deny / exit(2) AND Stop {"decision":"block"}, or hook-turn-end-gate drops out the same way. THIRD direction, against the installer's intent: every registry entry must also appear in install-reminder-hooks.sh's DESIRED block — verify-agentctl.py already parses that block as the system's canonical hook-intent source, so the registry is a SECOND hand-maintained list over the same domain, and an entry present here but absent there would make stage 3 warn about a hook the system never intended to install, on every machine, forever. Assert the subset relation in the same test module

doc.stages[1].means.method: Extract and generalize, don't reinvent: parameterize the existing matcher/command scan over (settings dict, basename) and drop the hardcoded Edit/Bash matcher pair. FIRST establish the real chain — read the harness's own settings precedence (docs/components/settings-and-permissions.md and, if it does not settle the order, the installed client bundle) and write the finding into the docstring; the chain logic is only as good as that check. The registry is a module-level tuple with a one-line note per entry naming what enforcement dies when it is absent — the same 'name the difficulty' discipline the hooks themselves follow. The reverse-direction registry test discovers blocking hooks by grepping the scripts/ tree for both block mechanisms rather than from a hand list, so the coverage claim is mechanical.
doc.stages[1].principle.derivation: The detector names the exact failure it exists to prevent, then reproduces it one level up: it reports all-clear from the system root while the live root is unguarded, so 'canon looks protected but isn't' is now true OF THE DETECTOR. A check is only evidence about the root it read; generalizing the probe and pointing it at the active root is what restores the evidential link.
doc.stages[1].principle.refutation: if a machine ran the agent system only through the claude-agent / claude-task launchers, the roots would always coincide and the old reading would be harmless — this machine's own live state (39 vs 20 hooks, transcripts under ~/.claude) refutes that as the actual usage
doc.stages[1].principle.source: hook-canon-guard-wired-check.py's own docstring — 'the guard silently not-enforcing is the worst failure mode for a read-only guarantee: canon looks protected but isn't'
doc.stages[1].principle.statement: A wiring detector that reads a different root than the one being wired is not a detector
doc.stages[1].subject.invariants: The probe is READ-ONLY and must never mutate any settings file — this task diagnoses, it does not install (the user's explicit scope decision). No import of agentctl from lib/: the probe is used by both a bare hook script and the engine, so it depends on neither. hook_wiring.py must NOT hardcode `Path.home() / ".claude"` — it calls stage 1's accessor. This is a booby trap, not a style preference: _PY_ROOT_TARGET_RE in test_config_root.py matches that literal and the new module is not in _LEGACY_REF_ALLOWLIST, so a hardcode goes red in a module THIS stage's verify_command does not run, surfacing only at stage 6 with two stages of work in between. UNKNOWN is a first-class outcome and the ONLY safe answer under partial information: a false ABSENT would make stage 4 emit a confident causal claim ('the hook is not registered in <root>') from evidence that does not support it — strictly worse than today's honest generic refusal. Verified on this machine while planning: ~/.claude/settings.local.json and the managed-settings.json BOTH exist and today declare zero hooks, so a single-file read is accidentally right here and would be wrong on any machine that wires a hook in either — which is precisely why the chain is modelled rather than assumed away.
doc.stages[1].subject.material: scripts/hook-canon-guard-wired-check.py lines 39-80 — _guard_commands_for / _script_path / check — which already implement this logic for exactly one hook against exactly one event pair; this stage lifts that logic to the general form rather than writing it fresh.
doc.stages[1].subject.result: New scripts/lib/hook_wiring.py answers, for a hook basename and a config root: is it wired at all, in which events/matchers, and does the script path it points at still exist on disk (the stale-worktree-path case hook-canon-guard-wired-check already handles). It scans EVERY event section (PreToolUse, PostToolUse, SessionStart, Stop, ...), not just PreToolUse. Critically it reads the settings CHAIN, not one file: the harness merges several members, so the probe enumerates them and returns ABSENT only when the basename appears in NONE of the readable members. THIS STAGE CREATES TWO NEW FILES (lib/hook_wiring.py and tests/test_hook_wiring.py) and its reverse-direction test greps the tree for block mechanisms — regexes, in a new module — so it mints crutch sites exactly as stage 5 does. It carries the task-wide staging invariant in full: git add both files, regenerate, re-stage the registry, and its verify command now runs verify-semantic-gates so the stage cannot report green over an obligation it created. A MISSING there is closed by regenerating AT THAT POINT, never by an implementation change. PRIOR ART, to be cited in hook_wiring.py's docstring rather than rediscovered: scripts/self-diagnose.py::default_settings_paths already enumerates six chain members using $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR else cwd. Note the asymmetry it exposes — the HOOK caller does receive CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR from the harness and so COULD locate the project member, while the engine caller cannot (verified: CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR is unset in the engine's environment). The decision below is therefore about what BOTH callers can answer identically, and the docstring should say so, leaving the project member as a documented extension for the day a project-wired gate-bearing hook actually appears. EXPLICIT MEMBERSHIP DECISION (this is a decision, not an omission): the chain is `<root>/settings.json`, `<root>/settings.local.json` and the managed-policy file — the USER-LEVEL members plus policy. Project-level `.claude/settings.json` is deliberately EXCLUDED, because neither caller can locate it honestly: the engine is invoked as `cd ~/claude-agent-instructions/scripts && python3 -m agentctl`, so a cwd-relative lookup inside gates.py resolves to `<repo>/scripts/.claude` and misses the real `<repo>/.claude/settings.local.json`, while the SessionStart hook runs with the session's own cwd — a third value again. Guessing that root is precisely how a false ABSENT gets manufactured. Consequently the ABSENT wording is QUALIFIED everywhere it surfaces: 'not registered in any user-level settings member of <root>', never an unqualified 'not registered'. Any member that is unreadable, or a settings shape the probe does not model, degrades the whole answer to UNKNOWN — never to ABSENT. The real merge order is CONFIRMED against the harness before implementing, and whatever is found is recorded in the module docstring; if it turns out one file governs after all, the chain logic collapses to a documented invariant rather than an assumption. The module also exposes the gate-bearing hook registry — the hooks whose absence silently disables ENFORCEMENT rather than merely dropping an advisory — as data, so a new gate-bearing hook is added in one place.

The check must not warn about ADVISORY hooks missing from the personal root: divergence is deliberate, and warning about the 7 advisory `*-due` hooks every session would train the user to ignore the whole warning — the registry's gate-bearing scope is what keeps this signal worth reading.

doc.stages[2].subject.result: hook-canon-guard-wired-check.py probes the ACTIVE harness root's settings chain instead of agent_home()/settings.json, and reports at session start EVERY gate-bearing hook from the registry that is missing from it — naming the root, the hooks, and what enforcement is consequently not running. It stays non-blocking and fail-open, as its docstring requires. Its $CLAUDE_CANON_GUARD_SETTINGS test seam is preserved, with its meaning made precise: the override designates the chain's PRIMARY member, and the remaining members are derived from that file's parent directory. This is what lets 'seam preserved' and 'chain modelled' both hold — today the seam is file-valued and all EIGHT existing test functions pass a file path (eight, not six — counted in test_canon_guard_wired_check.py), and under this reading every one of them is unaffected BY THE CHAIN CHANGE, because the sibling members simply do not exist beside their temp fixture. That is a narrower claim than 'they all still pass', and the difference matters to the executor: two of them assert stderr is EMPTY against a fixture that wires only the canon guard, so the moment the check WIDENS to the whole registry those fixtures legitimately produce warnings for every other registry hook and go red. That red means the FIXTURE needs widening to wire the full registry, NOT that the implementation is wrong — without this sentence the executor reads the red as its own bug and 'fixes' the widening back out. ONE-TIME ACCEPTANCE OBSERVATION, recorded here and NOT wired into the stage gate: run by hand against this machine's real ~/.claude root it must go from today's silent all-clear to naming hook-guard-canon-readonly and hook-plan-delivery-gate among the missing, and against ~/.claude-agent stay silent. That observation is environment-dependent — it stops holding on any other machine, and on this one the moment the personal root gains the hooks — so making it a verify_command clause would build a control that decays into a false red; it is evidence for the human at delivery, not a gate.

doc.stages[3].principle.derivation: The escape's author enumerated three distinct causes and gave the operator one undifferentiated exit. The engine can decide the 'uninstalled' case mechanically from observable state — it is a rule-part, not a perception-part — so leaving it to the operator to guess is determinization missing at exactly the level CLAUDE.md names. The operator's guess is also the expensive kind of wrong: the observed remedy was to take the escape, which is right for 'uninstalled' and wrong for 'the plan genuinely never reached the user'.

doc.stages[3].principle.statement: A fail-closed gate must be able to tell 'the proof is missing' from 'the prover is absent', or its refusal teaches nothing
doc.stages[3].subject.invariants: FAIL-CLOSED IS PRESERVED. The gate must not allow approval merely because the hook is missing — that would convert a fail-closed gate into one that any machine disables by not installing a hook, which is strictly worse than the current honest-but-opaque refusal. The escape stays human-initiated and audit-trailed; only its diagnosis improves. gates.py must not import a hook script — it depends on lib/hook_wiring.py only. AND: crutch_registry.toml's entry 6b802bd6c3ae8553 records, as its why-safe ground, that hook-plan-delivery-gate.py is regex-free across its FULL TRANSITIVE IMPORT CLOSURE, naming agentctl.gates explicitly. This stage widens that closure with lib/hook_wiring.py. The test compares id SETS only, so it stays green either way — which is exactly the danger: if hook_wiring.py carries any regex, that recorded ground becomes FALSE while still reading as audited. Either keep hook_wiring.py regex-free (preferred — settings parsing is json.load plus dict walks, no pattern matching needed) or amend that entry's ground in the same change. This is the plan's own 'a green that means nobody looked' failure mode pointed at the plan's own manifest.

The qualification is load-bearing HERE too, not only in the probe's own vocabulary: the earlier phrasing 'so nothing can produce the automated proof' asserted a universal negative the probe's evidence does not reach, since the chain deliberately excludes project-level members: run the task under claude-task / claude-agent (where the hook IS wired), or take the human escape. When the hook IS wired, or the probe answers UNKNOWN, the message keeps today's wording verbatim, because then the generic refusal is the honest one. The VERDICT is unchanged in every case: this stage changes what the gate SAYS, never whether it blocks. FORWARD-REFERENCE DISCIPLINE: at this stage the escape sentence names NO enum value, because the typed reasons do not exist until stage 5 — an operator who followed a reason name printed here would hit an argparse error. doc.stages[4].means.method: Add escape_reason to BOTH the dataclass (defaulted) and from_dict (via d.get) — the pair is the fix; either alone is the bug. Register --escape-reason in _ARG_DO_NOT_WRAP with its one-line why (an enum token, never a narrative path). For the inventory, do NOT claim to derive hatches from argparse by pattern alone — a pattern scan is a heuristic and calling it mechanical would repeat this task's own blind spot at a smaller scale. Instead declare _ESCAPE_HATCH_ARGS explicitly, mirroring the argv partition's proven shape, and make the pattern scan the REVERSE-direction test that catches an unregistered hatch, exactly as stage 2 does for the hook registry. THEN, IN THIS ORDER: `git add` every new .py file (escape-hatch-report.py, test_confirm_delivery.py, test_escape_hatch_report.py) FIRST, because the generator enumerates from the index and would otherwise be a SILENT NO-OP over exactly the files that need it; then run `python3 scripts/gen_crutch_registry.py`, never a hand-edit (the file's own header forbids it); then `git add scripts/crutch_registry.toml`. If any further .py file appears afterwards, re-run and re-stage — re-running over an unchanged tree reproduces a byte-identical registry (the generator's own docstring), so doing it more than once is free. This is not optional bookkeeping: crutch-inventory enumerates every git-tracked *.py under the root INCLUDING scripts/tests/ (verified: crutch_registry.toml is 16550 lines with 557 references to scripts/tests/), a scope becomes a site if it merely CONSTRUCTS OR REFERENCES A REGEX — no hard sink required — or if its name shares a token with {dispatch, route, spawn, suppress, emit, block, blocked, blockers, deny, select}, and verify-semantic-gates' MISSING condition has NO hard-sink filter: every enumerated site must carry a registry id. This stage's two new test modules do regex matching by construction, and escape-hatch-report.py's natural names in this repo's idiom (emit_*, select_*) are themselves in that token set — so new ids are minted here, and without the regeneration verify-semantic-gates (check 19 of 19) reds inside stage 6's verify-all, AFTER all six stages of work. New files need no per-entry authorship: they fall into existing partitions automatically (scripts/tests/** -> not-a-gate; scripts/lib/** and scripts/*.py -> structural). The new top-level script carries TWO obligations beyond its own code, both of which turn verify-all red if skipped and neither of which is obvious from the diff: a row in scripts/README.md's sentinel region (verify-readme.py globs scripts/*.py at the TOP LEVEL and diffs that set against the README — note the asymmetry that makes stage 2 clean: scripts/lib/hook_wiring.py is NOT globbed), and the executable bit BOTH on disk and in git's recorded mode (lint-hooks-executable.py covers every shebang-bearing script under scripts/, not only hook-*). Set the mode with git add --chmod=+x (the linter's own remediation string) if chmod alone leaves git's mode at 100644. Note the same index asymmetry applies here: lint-hooks-executable SKIPS the git-mode check when the file is untracked, so a green stage 5 does not prove 100755 in the index — the mode clause is unexercised until the file is staged, which is one more reason the staging step comes first.
doc.stages[4].principle.derivation: The escape was designed as a rare exception for a dead hook. It is in fact the majority path, and that fact was invisible for as long as the reason went unrecorded, because a free-text note is not aggregable. A typed reason turns each escape into a datum: 'hook_not_installed x N' is a work item, whereas N free-text notes are an archive nobody reads.

doc.stages[5].means.method: PROVENANCE FIRST, because principle/v1's rule is that a principle is never rootless: induced_from names memory-global/leaves/ask-user-question-split-turn — the existing leaf that documents this very delivery gate and its residuals, of which the unreachable-prover case is one made concrete here — and the experience leaf this task records at resolution is APPENDED to induced_from at that point, not forward-referenced now. If neither link can be made honest, the norm is not yet a principle and belongs in the README section alone; write it there rather than manufacturing a root. File the norm as a principle leaf, not as a CLAUDE.md edit: it is a design rule for whoever builds the next engine gate, not a per-turn behaviour the coordinator must hold in context, and CLAUDE.md carries a hard line ceiling that generic rules should not consume. Run verify-all LAST and in full. THIS STAGE INCURS A CLASS-4 OBLIGATION THAT STAGING CANNOT DISCHARGE, and it must be handled while writing, not discovered at verify time. verify-config-root-refs scans DOC scope — every tracked file whose suffix is not .py/.sh, so both scripts/agentctl/README.md and the new principle leaf — for `~/.claude` and `$HOME/.claude` (negative lookahead on '-', so `~/.claude-agent` is exempt), and any uncovered occurrence is a HARD FAILURE. Verified: agentctl/README.md carries ZERO such occurrences today, so a section about 'the two config roots' that names the literal would create the repo's first one. Two admissible resolutions, choose deliberately: (i) write the prose without the literal — '$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, else the CLI's own default root' — which costs some concreteness, or (ii) PREFERRED, name it and ship an allowlist entry in the SAME COMMIT (the allowlist header requires exactly that; an entry added ahead of its file reads as stale in every clean checkout, see 77ce06c), in anchored form `path:line:sha8` where sha8 is the first 8 hex of sha256 over the stripped line, with a mandatory reason carrying a category from the fixed taxonomy — `keep:harness-owned` is the honest one here, because the reference IS to the harness's own root. The file is `scripts/config-root-refs-allowlist.txt` (112 lines today) — the plan prescribed the row without ever naming it, which is the same declare-without-naming gap this stage's own criterion is about. Do NOT hand-compute the sha8: write the pin bare as `path:line` and run `verify-config-root-refs.py --repin`, which resolves a bare pin at a real occurrence to itself and mints its anchor automatically, staying consistent with the 85 pins already anchored — hand-computing invites a wrong anchor that reads as stale. Note also that stage 5 regenerates crutch_registry.toml BEFORE this stage writes the leaf, and that ordering is deliberate rather than an oversight: the registry's prose domain is outside verify-semantic-gates' code-only conditions so nothing reds, while regenerating AFTER the leaf landed would copy any bare legacy-path sentence into crutch_registry.toml — itself doc scope — and demand a SECOND pin there. The cost is that the registry ships without this leaf's prose rows; that is a known, harmless diff for whoever regenerates next. THEN, on reds: verify-config-root-refs (a red means either a genuine reference change to review OR, in this stage specifically, a new occurrence needing the row above — do not read it as a regression by default, which the earlier wording did), and verify-semantic-gates (check 19 — a MISSING/STALE red means the crutch registry drifted and the remedy is to RERUN gen_crutch_registry.py, never to hand-edit and never to 'fix' the implementation). The earlier version of this sentence predicted only the first and would have sent an executor hunting a nonexistent implementation bug; stage 5 now regenerates the registry precisely so this is a check, not a discovery.
doc.stages[5].principle.derivation: The rule this task induces is not something the coordinator applies every turn; it is a constraint on ENGINE DESIGN, applied when someone adds a gate whose satisfier is an external hook. Its reader is an author of agentctl, so it belongs in the engine's README plus a retrievable principle — filing it in CLAUDE.md would tax every session's context for a rule that fires a few times a year.
doc.stages[5].principle.refutation: if the norm turns out to need enforcing per-turn rather than per-design, it would warrant promotion to the instruction surface — the principle leaf is the retrievable form that makes such a promotion cheap

doc.stages[5].principle.statement: The norm belongs where the next author of the same mistake will be standing
doc.stages[5].subject.invariants: No CLAUDE.md edit in this task — an instruction-surface change is its own gated act via self-improvement, and folding it in here would smuggle a behavioural rule past that gate. Docs describe the divergence as DELIBERATE; nothing in this task installs hooks into the personal root.
doc.stages[5].subject.material: memory-global/leaves/principles/ and its MEMORY.md sub-index with the principle/v1 schema; scripts/agentctl/README.md as the engine's own contract doc.
doc.stages[5].subject.result: A principle/v1 leaf states the escape-hatch norm induced from this task: an engine escape hatch must (i) stay reachable, or a fail-closed gate bricks the spine; (ii) be preceded by a diagnosis that distinguishes a missing PROOF from an absent PROVER, decided mechanically wherever the engine can observe it; (iii) record a typed reason, not only free text; (iv) be counted, with a standing report making the count visible. The leaf also carries the second norm this task induced, which is about VERIFIERS rather than escapes and generalizes past this repo: when a checker enumerates its domain from one source (the git index) while reading content from another (the working tree), new artifacts are invisible to it and it answers OK for the wrong reason — a green that means 'not looked at' is worse than a red, and the fix belongs in the producing step (stage before you verify), not in the checker. And its sharper corollary, which is what the sixth and seventh review rounds cost between them: a checker can be index-ENUMERATED yet manifest-SATISFIED, so making an artifact visible to a checker is not the same act as satisfying it — surfacing an obligation never discharges it, and a plan that conflates the two produces a stage that is green precisely because nobody has looked. Pointer line added to the principles SUB-INDEX memory-global/leaves/principles/MEMORY.md under its matching Level heading — that is where principle leaves are indexed by convention; the top-level memory-global/MEMORY.md carries exactly one pointer, to the sub-index itself, and must not gain a second. scripts/agentctl/README.md gains a short ADDITIVE section on the two config roots — additive is a constraint, not a style note: doc-bindings.json binds three named headings in this exact file and verify-doc-concepts asserts they exist, so renaming or restructuring them reds check 19's neighbour, while adding a section is free (the verifier iterates the MANIFEST's concepts and has no reverse direction, so a new section incurs no registration obligation) and what the engine can and cannot enforce when they diverge — the doc an engine author reads before adding the next hook-backed gate. verify-all passes 19/19 and pytest sits at the main baseline.

doc.meta.goal: Fix two coupled defects in difficulty-channel routing. (a) scripts/difficulty_channel/detect.py classifies a machine as strong-internal (-> startrek) SOLELY because the `skotty` binary is on PATH (detect.py:50-51 appends 'skotty' to strong_internal unconditionally), even with no ~/.tracker-token and a GitHub remote — it only warns 'writes may fail' and never re-routes, so difficulty reports are pointed at a Startrek queue this machine cannot write to. (b) The report's SUBJECT LAYER (Core-system vs project) is honored on ONE channel only: file-difficulty.py:106 calls resolve_project_queue(target) inside the `channel=='startrek'` branch (project target -> its project queue, e.g. DEEPAGENT; Core -> OOSEVENREPORT), but the `channel in ('github','external')` branch (file-difficulty.py:124-127) NEVER consults the subject — a project-scoped difficulty is silently dumped into the single public Core GitHub repo with the same label as a Core difficulty. Fix: (a) demote skotty so it forces startrek ONLY when backed by a writable credential (~/.tracker-token) or an unambiguous corp marker; (b) make the github/external branch subject-AWARE — if the target resolves a project queue (subject==project) it must NOT be filed into the public Core repo: refuse with a clear message (the honest 'don't route where the channel cannot deliver' outcome), leaving Core-subject difficulties routing to github exactly as today. NOTE: `--layer` (ADR precedence core|team|personal, port.py:48) is a DIFFERENT axis from the subject and is deliberately left untouched; no vocabulary reconciliation is performed (port.py:48 is already correct).

doc.stages[2].means.method:
THE WINDOW, and why every scale shares it. Each actual is compared over the window that OPENS AT ARMING (cmd_approve), because that is the only window the estimate describes: the estimate is derived from the approved plan's stages, all of which execute after approval. A whole-session actual against a plan-execution estimate compares two different domains and produces a meaningless ratio — the reason the spend scale already excludes the main thread. Mechanically: `state.effort_baseline` is a snapshot of the actual vector taken at arming, and every comparison uses `actual - baseline`. This single rule is what makes the interactions and wall-clock scales sound; without it a pre-classify prompt or an overnight idle interval fires the trigger.

PER-SCALE ESTIMATE, derived from the CURRENT plan:
  spend      = sum of config.budget_usd(stage.actor.cost_tier or "medium") over `spawn:*`
               stages ONLY. in_thread stages are excluded from BOTH sides, because cost.py
               attributes no cost to them at all; including them in the estimate but not the
               actual would systematically deflate the ratio. A plan with zero spawn stages
               has estimate 0 and the spend scale is INAPPLICABLE.
  interactions = len(stages) + 1. Derivation, and it deliberately does NOT vary on
               acceptance-review stages: `StageReview.reviewer` may be an automated judge
               (`judge:haiku`, state.py:414-415), so an acceptance-review stage need cost no
               user interaction at all, while a stage boundary always surfaces one — the
               engine returns a directive after record-result and the coordinator's next
               dispatch is driven by the user's next turn. The `+1` is the terminal
               `resolve --by`. `approve --by` is NOT counted: it happens AT arming and is
               therefore in the baseline, not in the window.
  wall-clock = sum over ALL stages of effort-stage-minutes-<tier>, with in_thread stages
               priced at the small row (in_thread work consumes wall-clock even though it
               consumes no attributable spend — the one scale where the executor kinds are
               symmetric).
  replans    = structurally 0; this scale carries no ratio (see stage 2).
PER-SCALE ACTUAL, and where each comes from:
  spend      -> a NEW monotone field state.effort_actuals["spend_usd"], incremented in
               cmd_record_result by max(0.0, newly_attributed - previously_attributed_for
               _this_stage), where the previous value is read from the stage's own
               Outcome.cost_usd. The max() clamp is load-bearing, not defensive:
               cost.attribute_stage matches rows on (plan_path, stage_index) (cost.py:62-65)
               and cmd_replan REWRITES state.plan_path on both the refinement (cli.py:3154)
               and the substantive (cli.py:3182) branch, so a stage re-recorded under the
               new path attributes 0 against a non-zero prior and the raw delta is negative.
               Clamping keeps the accumulator monotone across a plan-path change; the spend
               already booked is never un-booked.
               It must be session-level and monotone, NOT a fold over state.stages: a
               substantive replan drops stages, and rollup_plan is literally such a fold
               (cost.py:93-100), so it would erase the very spend the brief's scenario
               depends on ("the accumulated actual keeps running").
  interactions -> a NEW field state.user_prompt_count, incremented inside
               hook-engine-start.py::_stamp_prompt_ts's existing patch (one extra key in a
               write that already happens on every prompt; best-effort, so a missed
               increment only under-counts).
  wall-clock -> a NEW monotone field state.effort_actuals["active_minutes"], accumulated in
               the SAME patch as ACTIVE time, not elapsed: on each prompt add
               min(now - state.last_active_stamp, substantive-wall-clock-min) and restamp.
               The cap is what makes it active rather than elapsed — a session left open
               overnight contributes at most one cap's worth, so idle time cannot fire the
               trigger. The cap reuses the existing substantive-wall-clock-min (30) with a
               stated basis: by the repo's own scale a gap of that length is a whole
               substantive task's worth of time and therefore cannot be one turn's thinking.
               `session_started_ts` is stamped once, if-absent, by the same patch, for the
               ledger row only — it is NOT the wall-clock actual. Alternatives rejected:
               (now - session_started_ts) counts idle time (the review's C3); state.history[0]
               carries no timestamp at all (state.log appends `{"event": ..., **fields}`).
  replans    -> len([h for h in state.history if h["event"] == "replan"]) — fully existing,
               and the same predicate cmd_resolve already uses (cli.py:2748).
FIRE RULE. Fire iff, for some scale with a non-degenerate estimate (> 0):
  (actual - baseline) / estimate >= effort-divergence-multiple, or for `replans`:
  (actual - baseline) >= effort-replan-absolute. There is no separate numeric floor; see
  stage 2 (e) for why, and for the arithmetic showing 5x of each scale's structural minimum
  reproduces the floors that were dropped.
RE-ARM, two belts, both required:
  (1) `effort_baseline` is REBASED to the actual vector at each firing, so the loop that
      would otherwise re-fire the moment the corrected plan is smaller than the accumulated
      actual is structurally impossible;
  (2) a fire additionally requires >= 1 `replan` event logged after the previous fire —
      the brief's "silent until a replan sets a new estimate" read literally.
  Both, because the rebase alone would let a fire recur at the next record-result if the new
  estimate were tiny, and the replan requirement alone would let it recur immediately after
  any replan. `state.effort_fires` records each firing (scale, ratio, ts, history length).
DELIVERABLES: `effort.estimate(state) -> dict`, `effort.actual(state) -> dict`,
  `effort.divergence(state) -> Divergence | None` (scale, actual, estimate, multiple, a
  one-sentence framing) as pure functions of state alone — no clock read inside the pure
  layer, since the time accumulation happens in the hook — plus `effort.rederive(state)`
  which recomputes and stores the estimate vector, and `effort.arm(state)` which rederives
  and snapshots the baseline.
Tests in scripts/tests/test_effort.py: each estimate derivation; the in_thread exclusion and
  the zero-spawn inapplicability; the baseline window (a pre-arming prompt and a pre-arming
  spend both fail to move the ratio); the idle cap (a 10-hour gap contributes <= 30 min);
  the monotone accumulator surviving a stage drop, a stage retry, and a plan_path rewrite;
  non-degeneracy-blocks-fire; threshold-blocks-fire; the rebase; the replan-required belt;
  and an AST purity assertion that effort.py imports no subprocess/socket.
doc.stages[2].principle.derivation: A fold over state.stages reads only stages that survive the replan; the brief's scenario deletes three of four stages, so a fold would report the actual of the one surviving stage against the contracted estimate — a ratio near 1 — at precisely the moment the true ratio is largest. Symmetrically, an actual counted over the whole session against an estimate derived from post-approval stages measures planning dialogue and idle time as if they were plan execution, which fires on every substantive task regardless of divergence. Monotone accumulation over an arming-relative window is therefore not a convenience but a precondition for the mechanism measuring anything at all.
doc.stages[2].principle.refutation: Construct a replan in which the dropped stages' spend SHOULD be forgiven — e.g. work genuinely handed to another task — and show the monotone accumulator produces a false fire there. If such cases are common, the accumulator needs an explicit transfer operation rather than pure monotonicity. Separately: if a task's real overrun regularly happens BEFORE approval (in planning), the arming-relative window hides it and a second, planning-phase window would be needed.
doc.stages[2].principle.source: The brief's recorded scenario ('the moment the user dropped stages 2-4, the remaining plan was worth ~$3 against an actual already far past it'); cost.py's own note that attribution is per-stage; and the thinker plan review's concerns 1-3, which found exactly this domain mismatch on the interactions and wall-clock scales.
doc.stages[2].principle.statement: An actual and an estimate must be measured over the same window and the same domain, or the ratio between them is not a measurement of anything — and the accumulated actual must be a monotone accumulator over that window, never a fold over the current stage list, because the exact case the mechanism exists to catch — a plan contracting under the actual — is the case in which the fold erases its own evidence.
doc.stages[2].subject.invariants: effort.py stays pure — no subprocess, no network, no filesystem, no clock — so tests/test_ast_purity.py's contract extends to it unchanged; no existing SessionState field changes meaning; a state file lacking the new fields loads with zeros (never a KeyError); hook-engine-start.py stays best-effort and silent on every error path, so a hook fault can still never wedge the workflow.

doc.stages[3].means.means: _diagnose_venue_refusal — the EXISTING VERIFYING -> DIAGNOSING router, reused verbatim in shape: `state.node = transition(state.node, 'diagnose'); state.difficulty = Difficulty(); store.save(state); return Directive(..., 'declare', marker='OVERCOME-DIFFICULTY')`. No new node, no new gate, no new terminal state, no new plugin.
doc.stages[3].means.method:
Q1 — CORE EDIT, option (b), NOT a plugin and NOT a hybrid. Three facts decide it:
  (i) plugins.py's scope fence (README § Plugins) forbids a plugin from introducing a new
      Node or gate; entering DIAGNOSING is a control-flow TRANSITION, which is exactly what
      the fence reserves for the core spine.
  (ii) a plugin observer runs in _fire_plugins AFTER the command has already computed and
      returned its Directive, so mutating state.node from an observer would emit a directive
      contradicting the state just saved — the same class of bug plugins_review_dispatch.py
      documents when it explains why it deliberately does not observe `replan`.
  (iii) the "coordinator must not be able to silently skip it" requirement is ALREADY met by
      the core transition alone: machine.TRANSITIONS gives DIAGNOSING exactly one outbound
      edge (`replan_refine`: DIAGNOSING -> VERIFYING) plus cmd_replan's direct set to
      PLAN_READY on a substantive replan, while `final` requires VERIFYING and `resolve`
      requires RESOLUTION. A session parked at DIAGNOSING therefore CANNOT reach RESOLVED
      without passing `replan`, which is itself gated on a complete difficulty record
      (gates.difficulty_blockers), normalization, failure-address and plan-review.
  Consequence, stated so it is not silently assumed: an obligations-ledger belt (a blocking
  PluginDirective registered in plugins_obligations._DISCHARGE) is REJECTED as redundant. It
  would buy no additional unskippability — the ledger only blocks the `resolution` gate,
  which is already unreachable — while costing a third _DISCHARGE entry and a forced update
  to verify-agentctl.py::check_obligations' static pin. Neither is spent.
FIRE SITES — both at node == VERIFYING, the only node from which `diagnose` is legal:
  1. cmd_record_result, immediately after `state.node = transition(state.node, "verify")` on
     the PASSED path: every actual has just been refreshed (cost attribution runs there).
     On the FAILED path the session is already entering DIAGNOSING, so the trigger does NOT
     transition again — it attaches its framing to the directive data and marks itself fired
     and rebased, because the terminal it wants (the difficulty cycle) is already happening.
  2. cmd_verify_final, before the `final` transition. This site is NOT optional: the brief's
     own scenario (a plan contracting to stages that already PASSED) reaches resolution
     without another record-result — finalize_partitioned (machine.py:60, fired at
     cli.py:2092-2100) reaches VERIFYING with no further record-result — so site 1 alone
     would never evaluate it. It is the last node at which `diagnose` is still legal.
  Both sites call one helper `_diagnose_effort_divergence(state, store, divergence)` modelled
  on _diagnose_venue_refusal, whose message pre-frames the declaration: actual effort exceeds
  the plan's re-derived estimate by Nx on scale S, therefore the plan's model of the situation
  is missing something — find what.
Q5 — RE-DERIVATION, per code path, each named individually because cmd_replan has NO shared
  tail (the branches save separately):
  cmd_approve: first arming — effort.arm(state) (rederive + snapshot the baseline).
  cmd_replan / `no_change` branch: after _apply_refined_stage_fields + _sync_venue_from_plan,
    before EACH of that branch's two save sites (cli.py:3132-3133 inside `if diagnosing:` and
    cli.py:3138-3139) — a single insertion covering only one of them silently leaves the
    other path stale.
  cmd_replan / `refinement` branch: before its own save at cli.py:3160-3161.
  cmd_replan / `substantive` branch: AFTER state.stages is replaced and PASSED stages are
    carried forward by stage_carry_key, before the save at cli.py:3182-3188 — the estimate
    must reflect the NEW stage list, which is the whole point.
  In all replan cases the ESTIMATE is re-derived and the BASELINE is left alone: the
  accumulated actual keeps running across a replan by design.
  A REJECTED replan early-returns WITHOUT store.save, so no re-derivation happens — correct,
  because the plan did not change. Named residual: an observer-based design could not have
  had this property, which is a second reason the wiring is a core edit and not a plugin.
SUB-PLAN CUSTODY — both cmd_push_subplan and PlanFrame enumerate their fields EXPLICITLY
  (cli.py:3300-3326 zeroes a listed set; state.py:700-722 snapshots a listed set), so a new
  field that is in neither leaks the parent's accumulated actual into the child and produces
  a guaranteed spurious fire inside every service sub-plan. Therefore:
  push: add effort_estimate / effort_actuals / effort_baseline / effort_fires to PlanFrame's
    snapshot list AND zero all four in the reset list; the child arms at its own approve.
    user_prompt_count and the active-minutes accumulator are session-level counters and are
    NOT zeroed — the child's baseline captures them at its own arming, which is what makes
    its window its own.
  pop: restore the parent's four fields, then ADD the child's consumption to the parent's
    additive accumulators (spend_usd and active_minutes) — effort spent inside a service
    sub-plan is effort spent on the parent's task, and forgiving it would hide exactly the
    overrun the brief describes. The child's replan count is NOT added (it is per-plan).
    Stated consequence, so it is not a surprise: a parent may fire immediately after a pop.
    That is correct behaviour, not a bug — an expensive sub-plan IS the signal.
THE BRIEF'S NAMED MITIGATION — extend cmd_resolve's quality_row (cli.py:2733-2757) with
  effort_estimate, effort_actual, effort_ratio_max and effort_fires. The brief makes "estimate
  and actual both land in the quality ledger" THE answer to the self-set-estimate weakness,
  and the floors-precalibration disposition rests on it; without this row the mitigation is
  described in prose and implemented nowhere, and the constants have no calibration path.
KILL SWITCH: `AGENTCTL_EFFORT=0` disables FIRING only, never accounting, so an exempted
  session still writes its ledger row.
Tests in scripts/tests/test_effort_trigger.py, driving the real CLI end to end: a session that
  overruns fires from record-result; a session that overruns only after contraction fires from
  verify-final; a fired session does not re-fire at the next record-result; it re-arms after a
  replan; a FAILED record does not double-transition; the rejected-replan path leaves the
  estimate untouched; each of the three replan branches re-derives; a sub-plan push/pop does
  not leak the parent's actual into the child and does return the child's spend to the parent;
  the quality row carries both vectors; AGENTCTL_EFFORT=0 suppresses the transition but not
  the row; and the pre-framed Difficulty declaration is present at DIAGNOSING.
doc.stages[3].principle.derivation: Reachability analysis of the table: RESOLVED is entered only by `resolve` (from RESOLUTION), RESOLUTION only by `final` (from VERIFYING), and DIAGNOSING's outbound set is {replan_refine -> VERIFYING} plus cmd_replan's direct set to PLAN_READY; therefore every path from DIAGNOSING to RESOLVED passes through cmd_replan, whose preconditions include a complete difficulty record. No second mechanism can strengthen a property that already holds by construction.
doc.stages[3].principle.refutation: Exhibit a command that writes state.node directly, bypassing `transition`, and opens a DIAGNOSING -> RESOLVED path. Three such direct writers exist today — `reset --force`, cmd_block/cmd_unblock (cli.py:3198/3209) and cmd_replan's substantive branch (cli.py:3188) — and none of them opens that path, so the conclusion holds while the basis is narrower than 'reset is the only one'. If a future command adds an edge out of DIAGNOSING, the graph argument weakens and a ledger belt becomes worth its cost.
doc.stages[3].principle.source: scripts/agentctl/machine.py TRANSITIONS (read in full) and README § Nodes' DIAGNOSING row: '`replan` is the sole exit and is precondition-gated on a complete Difficulty record'.
doc.stages[3].principle.statement: Unskippability is a property of the transition graph, not of a guard bolted beside it: because DIAGNOSING's only exit is a precondition-gated `replan`, moving the node IS the enforcement, and any additional blocking ledger entry is cost without effect.
doc.stages[3].subject.invariants: No new Node and no new entry in machine.TRANSITIONS; gates.py is not touched, so its purity contract and tests/test_ast_purity.py hold unchanged; plugins_obligations._DISCHARGE is unchanged, so verify-agentctl.py::check_obligations' pinned set needs no update; the FAILED path's existing behaviour is byte-identical; NO FIRE SITE ASKS THE USER ANYTHING — stated precisely, because the difficulty cycle a fire enters may itself reach PLAN_READY on a substantive replan, whose approval gate is a user interaction: that gate is the engine's existing behaviour for every difficulty, not a block this mechanism introduces, and the invariant is about the fire site and its directive.

doc.stages[0].means.method: Extend the pin regex to an optional third `:<hex8>` group; compute anchors with a single _line_anchor(text) helper; resolve each anchored entry against the file's occurrence lines before find_unallowed/find_stale_entries run, so both consumers see the resolved line; add --repin writing through a parse-preserving rewrite. ANTI-VACUITY: because --repin writes anchors with _line_anchor and the validator reads them with _line_anchor, a self-consistently wrong helper (whitespace mismatch, or degenerately constant) would make every downstream green vacuously — so one test pins the anchor definition against an INDEPENDENTLY computed literal: a hard-coded hex constant in the test body for a known line text, obtained without calling _line_anchor.
doc.stages[0].principle.derivation: The header states the pin's purpose is to force a re-read when the reference changes. A bare line number cannot observe the reference at all: it fires on any insertion above (no re-read value) and stays silent when the pinned line's text is rewritten while still matching the legacy pattern (re-read needed, none forced). Adding the content anchor makes the mechanism serve exactly the purpose the header claims for it, in both directions — which is why this is a strengthening, not a relaxation.
doc.stages[0].principle.refutation: if the repo wanted the pin to fire on ANY edit to the governing file, the anchor would defeat that intent — but the header names the reference, not the file, as the thing to re-read, and the whole-file escape form already exists for files where the ordinal is not the identity
doc.stages[0].principle.source: the allowlist's own header — 'Prefer the line pin: a stale pin forces a human to re-read the reference'
doc.stages[0].principle.statement: A pin whose identity is positional must carry the content it points at, or it cannot tell 'the reference changed' from 'something above it moved'
doc.stages[0].subject.invariants: An unanchored `path:line` entry must behave EXACTLY as today — the migration must be opt-in at the grammar level, not a flag day. Relocation is only ever silent-safe when the line text is byte-identical; anything else fails loudly. Never auto-rewrite the allowlist outside explicit --repin, and --repin must not disturb the existing accepted-and-ignored --staged flag or the no-flag path verify-all.py invokes. --repin rewrites IN PLACE, not from parsed entries: the 12-line comment header (lines 1-12, with line 13 blank), every blank line, and the raw two-space separator before `#` all survive byte-identical, or stage 2's diff review is worthless and the file loses its own documentation. ACCEPTED NAMED LIMIT: a byte-identical line cut and pasted into a DIFFERENT section relocates silently while a section-scoped reason (guards.md:48, :50, autocompact-threshold-policy.md:60 are worded that way) quietly goes stale. Anchoring over `nearest preceding heading + line` was considered and rejected: most reasons here are section-independent boilerplate (26 identical `keep:harness-owned` lines), so heading-scoping would churn the many to guard the few. The default-run relocation notice is the mitigation, and the limit is stated in the header rather than left to be rediscovered.
doc.stages[0].subject.material: scripts/verify-config-root-refs.py (329 lines: parse_allowlist / _covers / find_stale_entries / scan) and its 199-line test module. Enumerated and confirmed this session: these two files are the ONLY readers of the pin grammar in the repo — no hook, generator or worklist parses the allowlist, so the grammar extension has exactly one consumer to keep honest.
doc.stages[0].subject.result: verify-config-root-refs.py accepts a third pin field: `path:line:<sha8>` where sha8 is the first 8 hex of sha256 over the referenced line's stripped text. The candidate set an anchor resolves against is the file's OCCURRENCE lines — the lines find_occurrences already emits — never all lines of the file; that is the mechanism's own domain and it keeps ambiguity rare. Five resolution outcomes, each covered by a test: (i) anchor matches at the pinned line -> covered, exactly as today; (ii) anchor does not match at the pinned line but matches EXACTLY ONE other occurrence line -> RELOCATED: covered, not stale, not unallowed, and a notice naming old->new line is printed on the DEFAULT run (not only under --repin), so a reference that travels a long way is visible in the check's own output; (iii) anchor matches no occurrence line -> stale, the existing hard failure; (iv) anchor matches MORE THAN ONE occurrence line -> ambiguous, hard failure naming the candidates, never a silent guess; (v) cross-entry: two entries for the same file resolving to the SAME occurrence -> hard failure, because otherwise one entry silently double-covers while the other occurrence surfaces as unallowed with no stated cause. A bare `path:line` entry keeps today's behaviour byte-identical. A `--repin` flag rewrites the allowlist in place with relocated line numbers and freshly-computed anchors, preserving each entry's reason text verbatim.

doc.stages[2].principle.derivation: The norm 'run integrity checks after updating instructions' is fully decidable from an observable input (a pull applied commits) — it has no perception part — so it qualifies for structural mechanization. Placing it inside cmd_pull makes it fire deterministically on every applied pull regardless of which session/model triggers it, which prose cannot guarantee. Fail-open follows from the objective: a failed check is a signal to surface, not a reason to withhold the (already-applied) update.

doc.stages[2].principle.statement: Determinize a decidable norm structurally (wire the check into the pull command) rather than as prose the model may forget; fail-open so an integrity signal never strands the user without updated instructions

doc.stages[2].subject.result: sync-instructions-repo.sh gains a run_integrity_checks helper invoked in cmd_pull right before the final 'pull: done' log (so it runs ONLY on the reconcile path where commits were actually applied — the behind==0 early return at line ~132 and the fetch-not-found return at ~124 skip it, keeping up-to-date auto-pulls cheap; the stash-pop-conflict `return 1` at ~161 also bypasses it, acceptable on a conflicted tree). It runs (a) python3 verify-all.py for the GLOBAL layer, and (b) if the pull was invoked from a project holding .claude/agent-memory/MEMORY.md, python3 verify-leaf-structure.py --root <that agent-memory dir> for the PROJECT layer. Fail-open: each failure emits a loud log WARN line but NEVER aborts the pull — the helper is invoked as `run_integrity_checks || true` and each internal command is guarded, so set -euo pipefail cannot abort. The invocation directory is captured at FILE TOP into a variable BEFORE the module-scope `cd "$REPO"` at line ~30 (not inside cmd_pull); detached/cron runs whose cwd holds no project agent-memory skip the project check silently. A test in scripts/tests/ asserts the gate runs the global check after an applied pull and that a verify failure does not fail the pull (fail-open).

doc.stages[0].subject.result: scripts/self-diagnose.py: (a) _hook_script_path() resolves the script behind an interpreter-prefixed command — when tokens[0]'s basename is a known interpreter (python, python3, bash, sh, zsh, and `env` after skipping VAR=val assignments), it scans the remaining tokens for the first non-flag absolute path and returns that. Two fail-safe rules are explicit: (i) a candidate token CONTAINING WHITESPACE is rejected and never treated as a path — this is what keeps `bash -c '/abs/script.sh arg1'` from resolving to the whole quoted payload and false-flagging a working script as missing; (ii) when tokens[0] is ITSELF an absolute path, it is returned directly and the interpreter walk does not run, even if its basename looks like an interpreter — so the live `/Users/the0/.local/share/uv/tools/ccgram/bin/python -m ccgram.main hook` entry keeps today's behaviour (resolved to the interpreter binary, which exists, hence unflagged) rather than silently changing class. (b) default_settings_paths() additionally enumerates the agent config root's settings.json and settings.local.json via lib/config_root.agent_home(), keeping the existing resolve()-based de-duplication so a symlinked file is still scanned once. Both live dangling entries now appear as broken-hook-registration findings. scripts/tests/test_self_diagnose.py extended with cases for: interpreter-prefixed absolute script that is missing (flagged), interpreter-prefixed script that exists (not flagged), `bash -c` inline shell text (not flagged), `bash -c '/abs/path/script.sh arg1'` where the script EXISTS (not flagged — the whitespace rule prevents the false positive), `env VAR=v python3 /abs/x.py` with the assignment skipped (flagged when missing), an already-absolute interpreter with module args such as `/abs/bin/python -m pkg.mod hook` (not flagged, per rule ii), bare `jq` (not flagged), and agent-config-root enumeration.

doc.stages[1].subject.result: scripts/install-reminder-hooks.sh gains a prune pass and two flags. Ownership rule: an entry is OWNED iff its resolved script path lies inside $REPO/scripts/. The prune pass deletes an entry only when it is owned AND its script is missing; an unowned-and-missing entry is REPORTED to stderr and never deleted (a machine-local hook outside the repo is none of this script's business). A hook group left empty by a deletion is removed too, so no empty matcher stanza remains. The add pass keeps targeting the config root only; the prune pass runs over a HARD-CODED file list — the agent config root's settings.json/settings.local.json plus ~/.claude's — and deliberately does NOT reuse self-diagnose.py's default_settings_paths(), whose cwd-dependent project-local entry would let a prune run from an arbitrary cwd mutate an unrelated project's .claude/settings.local.json. Only the path-RESOLUTION helper from stage 1 is shared, never the file enumeration. The pass reuses the existing backup-before-write and JSON-validation path and the existing edit_ledger.stamp. Additionally this stage fixes the sibling defect in the installer's own basename_of(): it takes cmd.split()[0], so every interpreter-prefixed command resolves to the bare word `python3` instead of the script name, defeating the ADD pass's idempotency check — which is why duplicate hook entries have accumulated in both live files (measured: 5 duplicated (event, script) pairs of 39 entries in ~/.claude/settings.json, 3 of 45 in the agent config root). basename_of() is re-pointed at the shared stage-1 resolver so the add pass dedups correctly from now on. `--check` performs the same analysis, writes nothing, prints one line per dangling entry, and exits 1 if any owned dangling entry exists (0 when clean) so it can serve as a gate. Default invocation without flags stays behaviourally identical to today for the add direction. New scripts/tests/test_install_reminder_hooks_prune.py covers: owned+missing deleted, owned+present kept, unowned+missing reported-not-deleted, emptied group removed, --check exit codes both ways, backup written before mutation, basename_of() resolving an interpreter-prefixed command to the script name rather than to `python3`, and the add pass not re-adding an entry that is already present in interpreter-prefixed form.

doc.stages[0].subject.result: scripts/self-diagnose.py: (a) _hook_script_path() resolves the script behind an interpreter-prefixed command — when tokens[0]'s basename is a known interpreter (python, python3, bash, sh, zsh, and `env` after skipping VAR=val assignments), it scans the remaining tokens for the first non-flag absolute path and returns that. Two fail-safe rules are explicit: (i) a candidate token CONTAINING WHITESPACE is rejected and never treated as a path — this is what keeps `bash -c '/abs/script.sh arg1'` from resolving to the whole quoted payload and false-flagging a working script as missing; (ii) when tokens[0] is ITSELF an absolute path, it is returned directly and the interpreter walk does not run, even if its basename looks like an interpreter — so the live `/Users/the0/.local/share/uv/tools/ccgram/bin/python -m ccgram.main hook` entry keeps today's behaviour (resolved to the interpreter binary, which exists, hence unflagged) rather than silently changing class.
