doc.stages[1].subject.result: scripts/install-reminder-hooks.sh gains a prune pass and two flags. Ownership rule: an entry is OWNED iff its resolved script path lies inside $REPO/scripts/. The prune pass deletes an entry only when it is owned AND its script is missing; an unowned-and-missing entry is REPORTED to stderr and never deleted (a machine-local hook outside the repo is none of this script's business). A hook group left empty by a deletion is removed too, so no empty matcher stanza remains. The add pass keeps targeting the config root only; the prune pass runs over a HARD-CODED file list — the agent config root's settings.json/settings.local.json plus ~/.claude's — and deliberately does NOT reuse self-diagnose.py's default_settings_paths(), whose cwd-dependent project-local entry would let a prune run from an arbitrary cwd mutate an unrelated project's .claude/settings.local.json. Only the path-RESOLUTION helper from stage 1 is shared, never the file enumeration. The pass reuses the existing backup-before-write and JSON-validation path and the existing edit_ledger.stamp. Additionally this stage fixes the sibling defect in the installer's own basename_of(): it takes cmd.split()[0], so every interpreter-prefixed command resolves to the bare word `python3` instead of the script name, defeating the ADD pass's idempotency check — which is why duplicate hook entries have accumulated in both live files (measured: 5 duplicated (event, script) pairs of 39 entries in ~/.claude/settings.json, 3 of 45 in the agent config root). basename_of() is re-pointed at the shared stage-1 resolver so the add pass dedups correctly from now on. `--check` performs the same analysis, writes nothing, prints one line per dangling entry, and exits 1 if any owned dangling entry exists (0 when clean) so it can serve as a gate. Default invocation without flags stays behaviourally identical to today for the add direction. New scripts/tests/test_install_reminder_hooks_prune.py covers: owned+missing deleted, owned+present kept, unowned+missing reported-not-deleted, emptied group removed, --check exit codes both ways, backup written before mutation, basename_of() resolving an interpreter-prefixed command to the script name rather than to `python3`, and the add pass not re-adding an entry that is already present in interpreter-prefixed form.

doc.stages[0].subject.result: scripts/self-diagnose.py: (a) _hook_script_path() resolves the script behind an interpreter-prefixed command — when tokens[0]'s basename is a known interpreter (python, python3, bash, sh, zsh, and `env` after skipping VAR=val assignments), it scans the remaining tokens for the first non-flag absolute path and returns that. Two fail-safe rules are explicit: (i) a candidate token CONTAINING WHITESPACE is rejected and never treated as a path — this is what keeps `bash -c '/abs/script.sh arg1'` from resolving to the whole quoted payload and false-flagging a working script as missing; (ii) when tokens[0] is ITSELF an absolute path, it is returned directly and the interpreter walk does not run, even if its basename looks like an interpreter — so the live `/Users/the0/.local/share/uv/tools/ccgram/bin/python -m ccgram.main hook` entry keeps today's behaviour (resolved to the interpreter binary, which exists, hence unflagged) rather than silently changing class. (b) default_settings_paths() additionally enumerates the agent config root's settings.json and settings.local.json via lib/config_root.agent_home(), keeping the existing resolve()-based de-duplication so a symlinked file is still scanned once. Both live dangling entries now appear as broken-hook-registration findings. scripts/tests/test_self_diagnose.py extended with cases for: interpreter-prefixed absolute script that is missing (flagged), interpreter-prefixed script that exists (not flagged), `bash -c` inline shell text (not flagged), `bash -c '/abs/path/script.sh arg1'` where the script EXISTS (not flagged — the whitespace rule prevents the false positive), `env VAR=v python3 /abs/x.py` with the assignment skipped (flagged when missing), an already-absolute interpreter with module args such as `/abs/bin/python -m pkg.mod hook` (not flagged, per rule ii), bare `jq` (not flagged), and agent-config-root enumeration.

doc.stages[1].subject.result: scripts/install-reminder-hooks.sh gains a prune pass and two flags. Ownership rule: an entry is OWNED iff its resolved script path lies inside $REPO/scripts/. The prune pass deletes an entry only when it is owned AND its script is missing; an unowned-and-missing entry is REPORTED to stderr and never deleted (a machine-local hook outside the repo is none of this script's business). A hook group left empty by a deletion is removed too, so no empty matcher stanza remains. The add pass keeps targeting the config root only; the prune pass runs over a HARD-CODED file list — the agent config root's settings.json/settings.local.json plus ~/.claude's — and deliberately does NOT reuse self-diagnose.py's default_settings_paths(), whose cwd-dependent project-local entry would let a prune run from an arbitrary cwd mutate an unrelated project's .claude/settings.local.json. Only the path-RESOLUTION helper from stage 1 is shared, never the file enumeration. The pass reuses the existing backup-before-write and JSON-validation path and the existing edit_ledger.stamp. Additionally this stage fixes the sibling defect in the installer's own basename_of(): it takes cmd.split()[0], so every interpreter-prefixed command resolves to the bare word `python3` instead of the script name, defeating the ADD pass's idempotency check — which is why duplicate hook entries have accumulated in both live files (measured: 5 duplicated (event, script) pairs of 39 entries in ~/.claude/settings.json, 3 of 45 in the agent config root). basename_of() is re-pointed at the shared stage-1 resolver so the add pass dedups correctly from now on. `--check` performs the same analysis, writes nothing, prints one line per dangling entry, and exits 1 if any owned dangling entry exists (0 when clean) so it can serve as a gate. Default invocation without flags stays behaviourally identical to today for the add direction. New scripts/tests/test_install_reminder_hooks_prune.py covers: owned+missing deleted, owned+present kept, unowned+missing reported-not-deleted, emptied group removed, --check exit codes both ways, backup written before mutation, basename_of() resolving an interpreter-prefixed command to the script name rather than to `python3`, and the add pass not re-adding an entry that is already present in interpreter-prefixed form.

doc.stages[1].subject.result: Gap (a) — scripts/self-diagnose.py::_hook_script_path resolves the script behind an interpreter-prefixed command. It defines a module-level set named EXACTLY `_HOOK_INTERPRETER_BASENAMES` (this identifier is a binding contract: stage 5's landing instrument probes for it by name); when tokens[0]'s basename is in that set, or is `env` after skipping leading VAR=val assignments, the walk scans the remaining tokens for the first non-flag absolute path and returns it. Two fail-safe rules stay explicit: (i) a candidate token CONTAINING WHITESPACE is rejected and never treated as a path, so `bash -c '/abs/script.sh arg1'` does not resolve to the whole quoted payload and false-flag a working script; (ii) when tokens[0] is ITSELF an absolute path it is returned directly and the walk does not run, so the live `/Users/the0/.local/share/uv/tools/ccgram/bin/python -m ccgram.main hook` entry keeps today's behaviour. The preserved patch /tmp/cc-scratch/7a26998-interpreter-walk.patch carries a working implementation of exactly this, written against the pre-72b15f0 file; re-apply it as a fresh commit and adapt it to the current text rather than re-deriving it. Gap (b) — scripts/install-reminder-hooks.sh extends its PRUNE pass, and only its prune pass, to ~/.claude/settings.json. The script defines a shell array named EXACTLY `PRUNE_ONLY_SETTINGS` (also a binding contract, probed by name at stage 5) listing the files that receive prune-only treatment; today that is $HOME/.claude/settings.json. The ADD pass and the DESIRED table stay pointed at $CLAUDE_AGENT_HOME/settings.json alone — a prune-only file is never written to except to delete, never gains an entry, and is created if absent by nothing. Each prune-only file gets the same treatment the agent-home file already gets: backup to <path>.bak before any write, JSON validated before writing, edit_ledger.stamp on write, the unchanged ownership rule, and removal of a group emptied by its last deletion. A prune-only file that does not exist or does not parse is skipped with a stderr note, never created and never truncated. Tests: scripts/tests/test_self_diagnose.py gains cases for interpreter-prefixed-and-missing (flagged), interpreter-prefixed-and-present (not flagged), `bash -c` inline shell text (not flagged), `bash -c '/abs/script.sh arg1'` where the script exists (not flagged — the whitespace rule), `env VAR=v python3 /abs/x.py` missing (flagged), an absolute interpreter with module args (not flagged, rule ii), and bare `jq` (not flagged). A NEW file scripts/tests/test_install_reminder_hooks_two_file_prune.py covers: a dangling owned entry in a prune-only file is deleted, an unowned dangling entry there is left alone, no DESIRED entry is ever ADDED to a prune-only file, a backup is written before mutation, a group emptied there is removed, a missing prune-only file is skipped without being created, and an unparseable prune-only file is skipped without being truncated.

doc.stages[3].subject.invariants: English only. Respect the prose-length ceilings — no file may cross its lint threshold. Do NOT wire any live-settings check into verify-all.py: that suite must stay machine-independent and would otherwise fail on a clean checkout. On this stage's own control instrument: a verification instrument must be able to fail: an assertion that holds in both the done state and the not-done state is not an instrument. Probed before submission CONJUNCT BY CONJUNCT, not merely as a conjunction — a short-circuiting chain hides a vacuous earlier conjunct behind a later failure, which is exactly how the first draft of this command shipped a tautology: `prune-only` returns 0 hits in scripts/README.md (and 0 repo-wide across all markdown), `live machine state` returns 0 hits in docs/operations/guards.md, `install-reminder-hooks` returns 0 hits in memory-global/leaves/autocompact-threshold-policy.md (though 3 in README, which is why the leaf and not the README carries that conjunct), and lint-prose-length.py passes today. doc.stages[0].subject.result: scripts/self-diagnose.py: (a) _hook_script_path() resolves the script behind an interpreter-prefixed command — when tokens[0]'s basename is a known interpreter (python, python3, bash, sh, zsh, and `env` after skipping VAR=val assignments), it scans the remaining tokens for the first non-flag absolute path and returns that. (b) default_settings_paths() additionally enumerates the agent config root's settings.json and settings.local.json via lib/config_root.agent_home(), keeping the existing resolve()-based de-duplication so a symlinked file is still scanned once. Both live dangling entries now appear as broken-hook-registration findings. scripts/tests/test_self_diagnose.py extended with cases for: interpreter-prefixed absolute script that is missing (flagged), interpreter-prefixed script that exists (not flagged), `bash -c` inline shell text (not flagged), `bash -c '/abs/path/script.sh arg1'` where the script EXISTS (not flagged — the whitespace rule prevents the false positive), `env VAR=v python3 /abs/x.py` with the assignment skipped (flagged when missing), an already-absolute interpreter with module args such as `/abs/bin/python -m pkg.mod hook` (not flagged, per rule ii), bare `jq` (not flagged), and agent-config-root enumeration.

doc.stages[1].subject.result: scripts/install-reminder-hooks.sh gains a prune pass and two flags. Ownership rule: an entry is OWNED iff its resolved script path lies inside $REPO/scripts/. The prune pass deletes an entry only when it is owned AND its script is missing; an unowned-and-missing entry is REPORTED to stderr and never deleted (a machine-local hook outside the repo is none of this script's business). A hook group left empty by a deletion is removed too, so no empty matcher stanza remains. The add pass keeps targeting the config root only; the prune pass runs over a HARD-CODED file list — the agent config root's settings.json/settings.local.json plus ~/.claude's — and deliberately does NOT reuse self-diagnose.py's default_settings_paths(), whose cwd-dependent project-local entry would let a prune run from an arbitrary cwd mutate an unrelated project's .claude/settings.local.json. Only the path-RESOLUTION helper from stage 1 is shared, never the file enumeration. The pass reuses the existing backup-before-write and JSON-validation path and the existing edit_ledger.stamp. Additionally this stage fixes the sibling defect in the installer's own basename_of(): it takes cmd.split()[0], so every interpreter-prefixed command resolves to the bare word `python3` instead of the script name, defeating the ADD pass's idempotency check — which is why duplicate hook entries have accumulated in both live files (measured: 5 duplicated (event, script) pairs of 39 entries in ~/.claude/settings.json, 3 of 45 in the agent config root). basename_of() is re-pointed at the shared stage-1 resolver so the add pass dedups correctly from now on. `--check` performs the same analysis, writes nothing, prints one line per dangling entry, and exits 1 if any owned dangling entry exists (0 when clean) so it can serve as a gate. Default invocation without flags stays behaviourally identical to today for the add direction. New scripts/tests/test_install_reminder_hooks_prune.py covers: owned+missing deleted, owned+present kept, unowned+missing reported-not-deleted, emptied group removed, --check exit codes both ways, backup written before mutation, basename_of() resolving an interpreter-prefixed command to the script name rather than to `python3`, and the add pass not re-adding an entry that is already present in interpreter-prefixed form.

doc.stages[0].means.method:
(1) premise.py: add `OrderElement(id, element, disposition, stage, reason)` with `VALID_ORDER_DISPOSITIONS = {raised, covered, cut}`, plus `order_elements_from_dicts`/`order_elements_to_dicts` mirroring the existing round-trips. Add pure `validate_order_elements(elements, *, stage_indices, plan_present)` -> blockers: `raised` always blocks (the element was never dispositioned); `covered` needs a `stage` that is present in `stage_indices` (dangling-edge blocker, worded like the question one); `cut` needs a non-empty, non-placeholder `reason`; an unknown disposition blocks. UNLIKE the question bag, an EMPTY bag BLOCKS once `plan_present` is true — see [stage.principle]. (2) premise.py: add pure `render_coverage_block(elements, stage_count) -> str` producing exactly:
    [scope] plan has <N> stage(s); order: <M> element(s) — <C> covered, <K> cut
    - covered: <element> -> stage <n>
    - cut: <element> — <reason>
(covered lines in stage order, then cut lines in id order; deterministic, no timestamps). Stage 2 is its only other consumer — it is defined here so there is ONE generator, never a second hand-written rendering to drift. (3) plugins_premise.py: add `"order_elements": []` to `state_factory`, read it as `bag.get("order_elements", [])` (a bag minted before this change must load, not KeyError), and fold `validate_order_elements(..., stage_indices={s.index for s in doc.stages}, plan_present=bool(plan_path))` into `premise_blockers` next to the existing three families. (4) cli.py: add `order-raise --session --id --element`, `order-dispose --session --id --as covered --stage N | --as cut --reason <text>`, and `order-list --session [--format md]` (the `--format md` output IS `render_coverage_block`, so the coordinator pastes what the gate will check). Register them everywhere the `question-*` verbs are registered (COMMANDS, the plan-phase-allowed command list, the argparse builder, the shared arg-help tables). `order-raise` is permissive UPSERT like `question-raise`; `order-dispose` fast-fails on a missing `--stage`/`--reason` for its disposition (courtesy, not the authority — the gate is). `order-raise`'s `--element` help text says explicitly: enumerate FROM THE TEXT OF THE ORDER, before `submit-plan` — the mechanism cannot enforce that timing (residual named in stage 3), so the directive is where it lives. (5) scripts/tests/test_order_coverage.py: the pure validator table (each blocker rule, both directions), the CLI round-trip, and a gate-level e2e — a substantive session with a submitted plan REFUSES at `plan_approval` with an open element and ALLOWS once every element is covered/cut.
doc.stages[0].principle.derivation: The principle says a green that means 'I did not look' is worse than a red, because a red gets investigated. Apply it to the two bags side by side: an EMPTY question bag is honestly silent (a stage that needed to ask nothing asked nothing), which is why premise.py's docstring defends tolerating it — but EVERY task has an order, so an empty ORDER bag is not 'nothing to say', it is 'nobody looked', the exact state the prior task shipped in. The two bags therefore take OPPOSITE empty-set rules from one principle, and the difference is derived from whether the empty set can be a truthful observation, not from a preference for strictness.
doc.stages[0].principle.refutation: Refuted if fail-closed-on-empty proves unsatisfiable in practice — e.g. a substantive session whose order genuinely has no statable elements, or a recurring pattern of one throwaway element recorded purely to clear the gate (the decoy residual the premise leaf already names). Either would say the blocker buys ceremony rather than coverage, and the empty-set rule should revert to the question bag's tolerance with the discipline moved to the thinker review.

doc.stages[1].means.means: REUSE: `render_coverage_block` from stage 1 as the single generator; `cmd_present_plan`'s existing `--kind full` stage-anchor completeness check as the FORM (a mechanical containment check over engine-generated text, never a semantic read of prose — the `regex-not-for-semantic-classification` boundary); `gates.plan_presentation_active` and `state.plan_presentations[*].rendering_text` (already stored) for the gate half; the `question-dispose --to escalated` refusal as the precedent for a CLI fast-fail that is a courtesy while the gate is the authority.
doc.stages[1].means.method: (1) cmd_present_plan, `--kind essence` branch only: compute the block from the loaded plan doc + the active premise bag and require every non-empty line of it, stripped, to appear as a stripped line of the rendering text. On a miss, stamp NOTHING and return the block verbatim in the directive so the coordinator pastes it — the fast-fail exists because the essence is emitted as a turn's final message, so discovering the omission at `approve` would cost the whole present -> timer -> ask cycle. (2) plugins_premise.premise_blockers: when `gates.plan_presentation_active(state)` is true AND an essence receipt exists for `state.plan_path`, require that receipt's `rendering_text` to contain the CURRENT block; blocker names `present-plan --kind essence` as the route out. This is the half the fast-fail cannot do: it catches an element cut AFTER the essence was presented, which the plan_sha256 binding cannot see (the bag is not plan bytes). (3) Guard both halves so no unsatisfiable demand is created: silent when plan presentation is inactive (chat/small-change/AGENTCTL_PLAN_PRESENTATION=0) and silent when no essence receipt exists at all — that absence is already `gates.plan_presentation_blockers`' own refusal with its own route out, and double-blocking it would leave a refusal whose route belongs to another gate. (4) Element C rides the block's header line (`plan has <N> stage(s)`), so size reaches the user through the mechanism already being built rather than a second one. 'Expected volume' beyond the stage count is deliberately NOT mechanized: the engine has no honest source for a line/token estimate, and a fabricated one is worse than none — this is itself recorded as a CUT order element. (5) scripts/tests/test_order_coverage_essence.py: present-plan refuses an essence missing the block and stamps one containing it; the gate goes red when an element is cut after presenting and green again after re-presenting; both guards in (3) are proven silent.
doc.stages[1].principle.derivation: The corollary warns that a plan treating surfacing and satisfying as one step produces a stage green precisely because nobody has looked yet. Trace the two candidate designs against it: a present-plan-time check alone SURFACES (the block was in the rendering when stamped) but does not SATISFY (a cut recorded afterwards leaves the receipt's plan_sha256 valid, since the bag is not plan bytes, so approve passes over a stale cut list). Only re-deriving the block at gate time from live state closes that window — which is why the design carries BOTH halves and assigns the authority to the gate, not to the courtesy check.
doc.stages[1].principle.refutation: Refuted if the post-presentation-mutation window is unreachable in practice — if some other invariant already forces a re-presentation whenever the order bag changes, the gate half is dead code and the fast-fail alone suffices. It is also refuted from the other side if line-containment proves brittle against ordinary markdown editing (the coordinator reformats the block and the gate refuses honest work), which would push the check toward comparing a normalized projection instead of raw lines.

doc.stages[2].principle.derivation: The existing rule constrains one act (an ask) against one domain (the options the agent's own analysis enumerated), on the ground that a bound invented for internal economy must not silently become the boundary of the user's choice. doc.meta.done_criterion: BOTH network arms pass, because the user reported stalls on Wi-Fi as well as on mobile. Arm A, MTS mobile data with Wi-Fi off, VPN on: (1) Safari at ifconfig.me returns 81.22.132.183; (2) the YouTube app, with quality PINNED to 1080p in the player's own quality menu so adaptive bitrate cannot satisfy the check by silently downgrading, plays for >=3 minutes with no rebuffer stall; (3) the Instagram feed and Reels load and scroll; (4) Safari at fast.com reports >=10 Mbit/s. Arm B, the same four checks over home Wi-Fi. Then the freeze check: after 30 minutes of continuous VPN use on mobile data, checks 2-4 still pass — this is the only part that can catch the 120s/600s DPI freeze, which by construction does not show up in a short run. The threshold is 30 minutes. It is NOT lowered to 25 to match what was observed: the freeze model 600 s worst case would make 25 defensible on its own terms, but choosing it after seeing a 25-minute run is back-fitting, and the whole contraction of this plan rests on that run. So the record reads: threshold 30, observed 25, shortfall 5 minutes, knowingly accepted, and the +7-day follow-up supplying the coverage the missing 5 minutes would have bought. HONEST LIMIT: an INTERMITTENT symptom is not shown removed by one clean session, however long, and the original failing profile was NEVER re-tested under controlled conditions — the paired-trial control that would have done so was planned, reviewed and then removed on 2026-08-04 by user decision (reasoning in stage 2; it survives as standing lever R8). So the before/after pair this plan rests on is weeks apart, and intermittency explains that pair just as well as the configuration does. What this criterion establishes is exactly 'no stall observed in a continuous session on either network arm — 25 minutes against a 30-minute threshold, a recorded shortfall', and nothing about causation. Sustained absence needs a further week of ordinary use. That follow-up has a NAMED EXECUTOR and is not offloaded to the user: the agent schedules a +7-day wakeup at resolution time and runs the four checks then; recurrence inside that window reopens this task rather than opening a new one.

(1) Habr 1009542 'Как ТСПУ ловит VLESS в 2026 и почему XHTTP — следующий шаг': TSPU detection is 4-layer (signature / JA3-JA4 / active probing / behavioral); Reality's residual weakness is the post-handshake behavioral profile under load, and the recommended 2026 answer is VLESS+XHTTP+Reality with xPaddingBytes 100-1000 and a high-traffic SNI donor (github.com / twitch.tv / www.microsoft.com good; apple.com and niche sites bad because of cert-vs-ASN mismatch). (2) Same corpus: blocking outbound QUIC (udp/443) via a routing rule is the standard, widely-reported fix for 'YouTube buffers or will not load through the tunnel while ordinary TCP sites are fine' — the browser/app falls back to TCP+TLS. (3) onexray.com/docs: OneXray exposes Raw Edit / Xray Profiles / Full Config (replaces outbounds+routing+dns), real-time Access and Error logs, FakeDNS, DoT and On-Demand rules — but exposes NO TUN MTU setting, so an MTU hypothesis cannot be tested in-app and is deprioritised. (4) Project memory leaf project_vpn_setup.md (2026-06-30): confirmed-working combination is direct the0.fun:443 + Vision + fp=firefox; fp=ios is a named DPI signal; niche SNI ferzu.com is the unaddressed third signal. Reused: the memory leaf's confirmed link shape and the DPI three-signal model. NOTE, added at the 2026-08-04 contraction: the last sentence of this record described the PRE-CONTRACTION plan, which was to build a QUIC-block client profile and an XHTTP+Reality inbound. Neither was built — stage 1 selected no hypothesis and both stages were dropped. The research above is retained because it is what informed the discrimination, not because its remedies were adopted.

Otherwise compare three profiles: direct+Vision, direct-Vision, YC-Vision. If direct+Vision fails observation 3 AND direct-Vision carries YouTube on MTS -> the cause is the Vision traffic profile, NOT the entry path: drop flow= on the shipped profile and continue with the remaining stages, R1 not confirmed. The two YC-involving outcomes below apply only if the YC profile's own observation 1 returns 81.22.132.183 (a different address means the YC profile is not tunnelling at all and its YouTube result is meaningless — re-import once; if the second import still does not egress 81.22.132.183, record R1 as UNTESTED-BY-THIS-PROBE and proceed to branches (a)-(e), the direct+Vision / direct-Vision contrast above being unaffected). If direct+Vision AND direct-Vision both fail AND YC-Vision carries YouTube -> the failure is ENTRY-PATH-ATTRIBUTABLE (destination IP / ASN 199058 matching OR plain RU->NL transit quality — this observation does not separate those two, and does not need to, since the remedy is the same), which is R1's practical case: re-shape the plan around a Russian entry point WHILE RETAINING the SNI-donor change and the QUIC-blocking routing rule — NEITHER of which is in the current plan, since the 2026-08-04 contraction removed both; see R5 (donor), R7 (QUIC rule) and R1 (entry point) for where each went and why. They are independent of the entry point and R1 explicitly requires the donor change so a YC path would carry one DPI signal instead of three. Residual confound that no client-side profile can remove: the YC path is forced onto port 8443 (port 443 on that VM is DNAT'd to MTProto), so a non-standard TLS port remains an uncontrolled difference; record it rather than treating the branch as clean. Conversely, if the YC path fails at least as badly, this rules out the YC ENTRY POINT AS A REMEDY but does NOT close R1: the YC subnet is itself DPI-blacklisted (Signal 1 in project memory), the profile drops Vision and sits on port 8443, so a joint failure is equally consistent with both paths being blocked for different reasons. Record R1 as UNTESTED-BY-THIS-PROBE, proceed with branches (a)-(e), and if those also come back inconclusive, testing R1 properly requires a clean Russian entry point that is not the blacklisted YC subnet; (a) Safari at ifconfig.me does NOT return 81.22.132.183 -> H2 routing/DNS leak; (b) fast.com reports >=10 Mbit/s WHILE the YouTube app stalls -> bandwidth through the tunnel is healthy, so the fault is protocol-specific, which selects H1 QUIC and rules out H3; (c) YouTube plays in Safari but stalls in the YouTube app, and/or the OneXray Access log shows repeated udp:443 entries with errors -> H1 confirmed; (d) fast.com is low AND large pages in Safari stall after the first seconds -> H3 MTU/fragmentation; (e) everything passes on this short run -> NO hypothesis is selected and H4 is NOT excluded: hold the tunnel under continuous load for 30 minutes and re-observe. THIS THRESHOLD IS LEFT AT 30, the figure that was in force when the branch ran, and the run reached 25: a 5-minute shortfall, recorded as a shortfall. An earlier revision lowered the threshold to 25 and justified the new figure as 2.5x the freeze model 600 s worst case. That justification is sound in the abstract and was still back-fitting, because the number was chosen after seeing the observation and the entire contraction of this plan rests on that one run. Either accept the shortfall explicitly, as done here, or hold the missing 5 minutes; do not move the line to where the ball landed. The 30-minute hold is what the freeze model demands: it predicts failure only after 120-600 seconds, so a shorter hold cannot see one. Recorded as a written verdict naming the hypothesis and the observation that selected it, or naming branch (e).
doc.stages[0].title: Discriminate the failure mode on MTS mobile data
doc.stages[1].actor.capability_required: the user executing one field change in the 3x-ui panel; ssh to the0.fun for the reads (held)
doc.stages[1].conditions: Ungated on any traffic observation, because its justification is the 2026-06-30 DPI model rather than anything measured in this session — see the principle: editing a field Xray-core never reads cannot be validated or invalidated by a traffic result, so gating it on one would be a category error. Performed at a low-usage moment, since the SAVE restarts Xray-core and drops every live connection for a few seconds. HARD PRECONDITION: clients/stream-settings.before.json must already exist and hold fingerprint = ios BEFORE the user is given the panel path — verified present 2026-08-04. Once the panel saves, the pre-state is unrecoverable and this stage's done criterion becomes permanently unsatisfiable.
doc.stages[1].criterion.done_criterion: clients/check-inbound-diff.py exits 0: the canonicalised stream_settings fetched after the panel edit differs from clients/stream-settings.before.json in exactly one JSON path, realitySettings.settings.fingerprint ios->firefox, in nothing else beyond the tolerated class, AND the0.fun:443 still answers a TLS handshake afterwards. The runtime half is not decoration: the save restarts Xray-core, and a core that fails to come back leaves a perfectly correct database row while all seven clients are down — a DB diff alone would report green over a total outage. This is the plan's only irreversible server act and its only stage with no human watching the result, so it is the one that most needs a check on the axis that actually matters. The user re-reading the field they just typed is NOT the check either: a 3x-ui save re-serialises the whole blob, so privateKey, shortIds, serverNames and dest are precisely what must be proven unchanged. THE TOLERATED CLASS IS FIXED IN ADVANCE, in clients/check-inbound-diff.py itself, because once the panel has saved the pre-state is gone and any judgement made then is made against a sunk cost. A key that a differing 3x-ui version newly serialises (absent -> present) is tolerated and reported; a key that disappears, or an existing value that changes, never is — those are the shapes that silently rotate the keypair, drop a shortId or repoint dest. The script exits 2 with CANNOT VERIFY on an ssh or database failure, but exits 1 on a MISSING before-snapshot: that is not transient, and after the save it is unrecoverable, so retrying is the wrong response.
doc.stages[1].means.means: the 3x-ui web panel at https://the0.fun:2222/, executed BY THE USER, because the agent ssh account has no sudo password and a direct write to x-ui.db would be overwritten by the running panel, which holds the inbound in memory; unprivileged ssh plus sqlite3 against the world-readable /etc/x-ui/x-ui.db for the before and after READS
doc.stages[1].means.method: (1) CAPTURE THE BEFORE-STATE FIRST, before the user is given the panel path: ssh the0.fun sqlite3 select stream_settings from inbounds where id=1, canonicalised through json.dumps(sort_keys=True, indent=2) into clients/stream-settings.before.json. Once the user saves in the panel the pre-state is unrecoverable and this done criterion becomes permanently unsatisfiable, degrading silently back into the user re-reading their own typing. DONE 2026-08-04; the file exists. (2) Hand the user the panel path and the one field to change, with the instruction to do it at a low-usage moment. (3) Run clients/check-inbound-diff.py, which re-fetches, canonicalises identically and compares structurally — key order and whitespace differ across a 3x-ui re-serialisation, so a textual diff would report noise.
doc.stages[1].principle.derivation: Because Xray-core ignores realitySettings.settings, editing it changes NOTHING about the running tunnel: it changes only what the panel writes into future links. So the edit cannot be validated or invalidated by a traffic observation, and gating it on one is a category error — the recurrence it prevents is a future link carrying fp=ios, not a current stall. The SAVE ACTION is a separate matter and does restart the core; see invariants.
doc.stages[1].principle.refutation: If the after-dump shows realitySettings.settings.fingerprint unchanged while the panel UI displays firefox, the field being edited is not the one that feeds link generation, and the panel is writing somewhere this plan has not located
doc.stages[1].principle.source: 3x-ui realitySettings.settings block, which Xray-core does not consume server-side and which exists solely to generate client links; project memory leaf project_vpn_setup.md (2026-06-30) naming fp=ios as Signal 2
doc.stages[1].principle.statement: Correcting the links without correcting the inbound fingerprint field leaves the panel free to regenerate the original defect on the next link it issues, so the edit is justified by the panel future behaviour rather than by any observation in this session — which is why it must not be gated on an observation
doc.stages[1].subject.invariants: The Reality keypair, shortIds, serverNames and dest are not touched, so no existing LINK is invalidated and no client needs to re-import on a deadline. That is NOT the same as no service interruption: a 3x-ui inbound save restarts Xray-core and drops every live connection for a few seconds, which is why this is timed rather than done on demand. MTProto on 8443 and the panel on 2222 are untouched.
doc.stages[1].subject.material: inbound id=1 stream_settings.realitySettings.settings.fingerprint on the0.fun, which currently reads ios
doc.stages[1].subject.result: Inbound id=1 on the0.fun has realitySettings.settings.fingerprint set to firefox rather than ios, and a before/after dump of that inbound stream_settings differs in exactly that one JSON path and in nothing else. This is a SEPARATE stage from the link distribution. An intermediate revision of this plan placed a paired-trial control between them — four alternating >=11-minute runs of the original profile against the corrected one — to test whether the three-field change was actually the operative variable. It was REMOVED on 2026-08-04, and the removal is a real evidential loss recorded as such rather than talked away: the attribution stays a hypothesis, exactly as clients/corrected-links.md already states in its header. ONE reason carries the removal, and the others are kept separate from it on purpose. THE CARRYING REASON: the control would have cost roughly 50 minutes of the user's attention, spent against a symptom that is not currently reproducing — and a trial run without a live symptom is close to powerless on its A arm, since a clean A run means only that nothing happened to be wrong that minute. Bad price, bad moment. TWO FURTHER FAULTS the same review found, which are NOT reasons to delete the instrument and are recorded as what they are so that nobody later reads them as having retired it: the gate sat in the wrong place, protecting the reversible half (handing out links, re-import optional per client, revertible by re-importing the old one) while the one irreversible act — this panel save, which restarts Xray-core for all seven clients — sat outside it; and a null result was wired to cancel the six-client distribution, which does not follow, because the fp=ios ground for reissuing comes from the 2026-06-30 DPI model and holds whatever a trial says. Those two argue for MOVING the gate and REWIRING the outcome, and the plan did both: the distribution stage is now ungated and the panel edit carries a runtime check. They do not argue for removing the trial, and no claim is made here about how the trial would most likely have come out — nobody knows. The paired trial survives as standing lever R8: it is the FIRST instrument to reach for if the symptom returns, and it is cheaper then, because a live symptom is what makes an A-arm run informative in the first place. The justification for it does not come from this session evidence at all: fp=ios is named as Signal 2 in the recorded three-signal DPI model from 2026-06-30, independently of whether the paired trial reproduces anything, and the panel will keep stamping ios into every link it issues until the field is changed. An earlier revision buried this edit inside the link-distribution stage, where a gate it was never meant to be under could have left the plan's one irreversible server operation executable with no stage, no gate, and no run of the checker that verifies it. Splitting it out is the fix, and it outlived the gate that prompted it.
doc.stages[1].title: Stop the panel emitting fp=ios
doc.stages[2].actor.capability_required: ssh to the0.fun for the reads (held); a channel to reach the six other clients
doc.stages[2].conditions: UNGATED, and the reasoning that removed the gate is recorded in stage 2. Handing a client a link is reversible for that client alone — re-import is optional and at leisure, and the old profile stays on the phone as a working fallback — so the blast radius of being wrong is one re-import per person, not a broken window. What the six are told is therefore load-bearing, and it is set by the header of corrected-links.md: these links carry a change whose effect is a hypothesis, not a demonstrated fix, and the six have LESS evidence behind them than rpqowix2 does, because their stored flow is empty so they carry no Vision. Distributing them silently as 'the fix' would be the dishonest version of this stage. Stage 1 recorded that the profile which PASSED differs in three fields (host / fp / sni) from the profile the user reported failing before this session, and that branch (a0)->(e) selected NO hypothesis — so nothing was attributed to a single field, and no failure was reproduced. All three are corrected together; fp=ios leads only because project memory names it Signal 2, and R3 carries that limit. The x-ui client table is readable over the existing unprivileged ssh account.
doc.stages[2].criterion.done_criterion: clients/check-links.py exits 0: it reads the live inbound over ssh and asserts, per link, that uuid and flow match that client stored row, that the endpoint is the0.fun:443 for the six and either form for rpqowix2 — the split is enforced by the checker, not merely described in prose — that sid and sni are in realitySettings.shortIds and realitySettings.serverNames, and that pbk equals the X25519 public key DERIVED from realitySettings.privateKey. Derivation, not a read of realitySettings.settings.publicKey: this plan own stage-2 principle states that Xray-core never consumes that nested block, which is also why the fingerprint edit is a separate stage, so comparing a link to it proves only that the link agrees with what the panel displays — the same non-check as a user re-reading what they just typed, which this plan rejects one sentence later for the fingerprint. A publicKey that has drifted from the private key fails the handshake for all seven at once with no diagnostic, and only derivation catches it. The X25519 implementation self-tests against the RFC 7748 section 6.1 vector on EVERY run, inside check-links.py, rather than having been checked once by hand: gen-links.py imports that same derivation, so a bug in it would write consistently wrong pbk values into the links AND pass the checker green — the silent all-seven handshake failure that reading the panel publicKey was rejected for, reintroduced through the shared-code shortcut. pbk is compared as decoded BYTES, not as a string, so a link written in the standard base64 alphabet is not misreported as a key mismatch. Recorded cross-check 2026-08-04: the derived key matched 3x-ui own independently computed publicKey, so panel and private key are in sync today; the private key is read into memory, never printed and never passed on a command line. security and type ARE asserted against the live stream_settings.security and stream_settings.network, with tcp and raw treated as one transport because Xray renamed it in v25.x while x-ui still stores the old spelling — leaving them constant would let seven links pass green against an inbound whose transport had been changed underneath them. Only TWO fields are compared to constants: the endpoint policy, which this plan defines rather than the server, and fp, which cannot be server-asserted because the live fingerprint field is itself the thing under repair and reads ios until the panel edit lands, so asserting the links against it would invert the check. AND clients/check-distribution.py exits 0: distribution.md records, for each of the six, a handover date, a channel, caveat-sent=yes and the uuid tail — not merely the client name, because a file listing all six as not-yet-sent would otherwise satisfy a name-only grep, and not merely a non-empty caveat cell, because one reading 'no' would then pass a check whose entire purpose is that the caveat travelled. That checker is a committed script with its own --self-test rather than an inline grep pattern: two defects (a caveat column that accepted 'no', a channel class that rejected Cyrillic and so would have failed a correct log written in the operator's own language) survived inside the quoting layers of the shell one-liner it replaces, which is what an untestable check buys. NOTE on transport, a deliberate asymmetry: check-links.py treats tcp and raw as one transport, while gen-links.py REFUSES to generate unless the live inbound reads raw. The checker must accept a correct link whatever spelling the server stores; the generator is choosing what to write and should stop rather than guess if the server no longer looks the way this plan assumes. The asymmetry is safe in the direction it fails. check-links.py exits 2 with CANNOT VERIFY on an ssh, schema or database failure, so an infrastructure outage is never readable as a link mismatch. A failed RFC 7748 self-test is deliberately NOT in that class and exits 1: it is deterministic and will fail identically forever, so retrying is the wrong response.
doc.stages[2].criterion.verify_command: L=/Users/the0/projects/yandex-cloud/clients/corrected-links.md; test -f $L && test $(grep -c '^vless://' $L) -eq 7 && test $(grep -c '^vless://.*flow=' $L) -eq 1 && test $(grep -c '^vless://.*flow=xtls-rprx-vision' $L) -eq 1 && test $(grep -c '^vless://.*fp=firefox' $L) -eq 7 && test $(grep -c '^vless://.*sni=www[.]ferzu[.]com' $L) -eq 7 && ! grep -q '^vless://.*fp=ios' $L && python3 /Users/the0/projects/yandex-cloud/clients/check-distribution.py --self-test && python3 /Users/the0/projects/yandex-cloud/clients/check-distribution.py && python3 /Users/the0/projects/yandex-cloud/clients/check-links.py
doc.stages[2].means.means: unprivileged ssh to the0.fun plus sqlite3 against the world-readable /etc/x-ui/x-ui.db for READING the client table; the committed generator clients/gen-links.py, which reads the live inbound and emits the file, and which imports check-links.py server reader and key derivation rather than duplicating them, so generator and checker cannot drift apart
doc.stages[2].means.method: Three steps, and only the third leaves this machine. The before-snapshot capture that an earlier revision listed here as step (1) belongs to stage 2 and is not repeated: it was listed in both places while the artifacts were produced in one sitting, which is two places to keep in sync and one to forget. (1) Read the seven client rows (email, uuid, flow) from the inbound settings JSON and emit one link per client, asserting sid and sni against the live realitySettings and pbk against the key derived from realitySettings.privateKey, rather than against constants transcribed into the generator — a wrong pbk fails the handshake for all seven at once with no diagnostic. The generator clients/gen-links.py is committed rather than being a one-off inline script, so R3 documented repair (regenerate rpqowix2 against the hostname) is a one-line policy change plus a re-run, not a hand-edit of seven near-identical 200-character URLs, which is precisely how a uuid gets paired with the wrong client. Copy flow and uuid verbatim per client; use the literal IP only for rpqowix2. (2) Write the file with a header stating what was verified, on which client, and what was not, so the untested six do not read as covered by the tested one. (3) DISTRIBUTE the six other clients their links. Recorded in clients/distribution.md, one row per client — email, the date handed over, the channel, whether the caveat travelled in that message, and whether the client confirmed the new link connects. The caveat column exists because conditions call sending these out silently as 'the fix' the dishonest version of this stage, and a requirement with no carrier and no column is a requirement that quietly does not happen. Until that file exists the six have been given nothing, whatever corrected-links.md contains — a link sitting in a repo is not a link a client has, and conflating the two is how a distribution stage reports itself done without anyone having received anything. The panel write is stage 2 and is not performed here.
doc.stages[2].principle.derivation: XTLS Vision is negotiated, not merely advertised: the server accepts the flow the client declares only if the matching client entry declares it too, so writing flow=xtls-rprx-vision into a link whose stored entry holds the empty string produces a connection failure rather than a downgrade. That makes per-client copying the only correct generation rule, and it is why the generator reads flow per client from the live table rather than taking a single flag.
doc.stages[2].principle.refutation: If a reissued link fails for a client whose flow was copied verbatim, the mismatch model is wrong and the difference lies in a field this stage held fixed — most likely uuid drift between the settings JSON and the live config, which would be visible as an auth failure in the server's Xray error log
doc.stages[2].principle.source: the live x-ui client table read 2026-08-04 (six of seven clients store an empty flow); Xray-core VLESS docs on flow matching
doc.stages[2].principle.statement: A client link is only valid if every field it declares is consistent with the server-side entry it authenticates against, so flow must be copied from each client stored value rather than generalised from the one client that was tested
doc.stages[2].subject.invariants: EACH CLIENT RECEIVES THEIR OWN LINK AND NOTHING ELSE. clients/corrected-links.md is NOT the delivery artifact and is never forwarded whole: a VLESS uuid IS the client's only authentication secret, and the file holds all seven alongside the shared pbk, sid and sni, so every line in it is a complete working credential. Sending the file to the six would hand every one of them everyone else's access, which destroys the only thing seven separate client entries buy — per-person accounting and per-person revocation — and it is not undoable: the sole remedy is rotating a uuid, i.e. a forced re-import with no working fallback, exactly the break R5 refuses to inflict for the SNI donor. It also removes the ground this stage stands on: conditions call the blast radius of being wrong 'one re-import per person, not a broken window', and that is true only of per-client delivery. Copy the one line whose #fragment names that client, and carry the caveat in the message body — the file header does not travel with a single copied line, so the honesty requirement in conditions has no carrier unless it is restated per message. No client's flow= is invented — a link may carry flow=xtls-rprx-vision only if that client's server-side flow field already holds it, because a mismatch between the link and the stored client entry breaks the connection outright. A link's uuid is never generalised across clients either: a mis-paired uuid still parses and still authenticates, so the error is silent, and pairing it with the wrong flow produces the hard mismatch above with nothing pointing at the cause. The Reality keypair, shortIds, serverNames and dest are not touched, so no existing LINK is invalidated and no client needs to re-import on a deadline. This stage performs NO server write at all: it hands out links. The Xray-core restart belongs to stage 2, the panel edit.
doc.stages[2].subject.material: the seven client entries stored in inbound id=1 of /etc/x-ui/x-ui.db (rpqowix2 with flow=xtls-rprx-vision; ser6nzfgq, v1xlgcwj, e3ebuxsw, s1r2nxde, wfu2tc1m, mb7fi0ri all with flow set to the empty string)
doc.stages[2].subject.result: File clients/corrected-links.md exists under the repo root and carries one VLESS link per client for all seven x-ui client entries. Every link differs from what the panel issues today in the fields that separate the profile which PASSED stage 1 from the profile the user reported failing BEFORE this session — a failure never re-observed under controlled conditions, so 'correction' is the intent of the change and not a demonstrated property of it — fp=firefox instead of fp=ios, and sni=www.ferzu.com instead of sni=ferzu.com. A third field differs for ONE client only: rpqowix2 carries the literal 81.22.132.183 because that is what the profile which actually passed carried, while the other six carry the0.fun, which is both what project memory records as the confirmed form and what keeps a future VPS-IP change from silently breaking all seven at once. Every link's flow= matches that client's server-side flow value EXACTLY (present only for rpqowix2, absent for the other six, whose stored flow is the empty string), and every link's uuid matches the client named in its own #fragment. The three fields are corrected TOGETHER and NO single-field attribution is claimed: fp=ios leads only because project memory names it Signal 2. AND the six have actually been handed their links: clients/distribution.md exists and carries, per client, a handover date, the channel it went through, an explicit record that the caveat travelled in that message, and the last four characters of the uuid actually sent. All four are gated by clients/check-distribution.py, so the result image names all four rather than the first two: an image weaker than the criterion invites a stage-boundary check that passes on an image nobody stated. That second half is part of the result image and not only of the criterion, because this plan says elsewhere that a link sitting in a repo is not a link a client has — a result image that stops at the generated file would let a stage-boundary check pass over seven links nobody received, which is the exact confusion the criterion was written to catch. The fingerprint half of what used to be this stage now lives in stage 2, which this stage neither depends on nor performs: nothing here reads the panel, the fp value is a constant in gen-links.py, and the links are handed out from a file. Sequencing the two is a convenience, not a dependency.
